A small piece of heaven for a family broken by tragedy. In July, Sierra Sharry was eight months pregnant and about to become a mother. Her partner, Lane Smith, fell and hit his head. He was taken to OU Medical Center in Oklahoma City, but he never woke up. "July 13th, 2014 was the absolute worst day of my life," Sharry wrote on Facebook. "I lost my best friend. The father of my unborn child." Their son, Taos, was born a few weeks later. When it was time for his 6-month photo, Sharry asked the photographer if they could somehow make their family feel complete, just for one picture.

You probably already have an opinion about Indiana's religious freedom law. Some people support the growing number of companies that criticize the law, saying it lets businesses turn away gay and lesbian people by claiming religion. Others, like Indiana Governor Mike Pence, are surprised by the anger. They say the law is similar to one already used at the federal level and in 19 other states. This debate causes division because arguments over religious freedom and gay rights are always emotional. It's also hard to trust the law’s true meaning and purpose.

Some fans of Lucille Ball want her statue removed from a park in her hometown, Celoron, New York. They say the statue looks ugly and doesn't match the "I Love Lucy" star. The life-size bronze statue has been compared to singer Conway Twitty, the snake from "Beetlejuice," and actor Steve Buscemi—among other unflattering looks. Even Celoron's mayor, Scott Schrecengost, has said he doesn't like the statue. It shows Lucille Ball holding a bottle of the fictional drink Vitameatavegamin. But despite the criticism, the statue has drawn tourists since 20009. People visit Celoron to take pictures with it.

The last time Muhammadu Buhari became president of Nigeria, he took power by force. This time, he won through a fair election. These are five reasons why this election, one of the most heated in Nigeria’s history, matters so much. For the first time, the opposition party beat the ruling party in a democratic vote. Buhari, who is 77, won the presidential election by about two million votes, beating the current president, Goodluck Jonathan. Nigeria is important because it is Africa’s largest economy and most populous country. It is also one of the continent’s top oil producers and a major source of crude oil for the United States.

People in Iran were extremely excited, almost like they had won a big international game. But this was even more important. Iranians celebrated after a major nuclear agreement was reached with the United States and other countries. The deal could end years of tough international sanctions and Iran’s isolation from the global community. Late Thursday night, in Tehran’s Vali Asr Street, people filled the streets. Cars honed their horns, men danced in the middle of traffic, people waved flags from car roofs, played loud music, and shared messages online using the hashtag #IranTalks. Some even showed off U.S. dollars, showing their joy and hope for a new future.

A fourth man, Dilkhayot Kasimov, has been charged in a Brooklyn federal court indictment related to a plot to support terrorists and help some of the men join ISIS. The indictment was released on Monday. The three other men — Abdurasul Hasanovich Juraboev, Akhror Saidakhmetov, and Abror Habibov — were already charged with two counts of supporting a foreign terrorist organization. They have all pleaded not guilty. It is not known whether Kasimov has been arrested.

CNN reported that the third blood moon in a four-part series was the shortest eclipse of the group. It happened early on Saturday morning. The moon fully entered Earth's shadow at 4:58 a.m. Pacific Time (7:58 a.m. ET). This caused a total lunar eclipse that lasted just under five minutes — the shortest total lunar eclipse this century, according to NASA. The moon turned a burnt-orange color before, during, and after the eclipse. This orange glow is why total lunar eclipses are called "blood moons."

Istanbul, Turkey (CNN)  
On Tuesday, many Turks were scared and confused. An older woman wearing a white headscarf and carrying shopping bags stood outside a busy subway station, asking, "What's happening? Why can't I get in?" She was one of millions affected by the worst power outage in Turkey in over ten years. Dozens of cities across the country lost electricity for several hours. Millions of people were impacted, including passengers stuck on stopped trains and subtrains.

During this Holy Week, let’s remember what God’s word says about fair wages and justice. The Bible says that true fasting means breaking unfair chains, ending workplace abuse, freeing those who are oppressed, and forgiving debts. McDonald’s decision to raise wages for 90,0000 workers is a big win for fast-food cooks and cashiers, and for everyone who supports them. When fast-food workers stand together, they are making it harder for rich companies like McDonald’s to pay wages so low that workers can’t get by.

California may soon be known for the color of its lawns—brown. Governor Jerry Brown has ordered mandatory water cuts for the first time. Cities, towns, businesses, and farms must cut water use by 25. This means saving about 1.5 million acre-feet of water over the next nine months. An acre-foot is about 325,000 gallons. Brown said this marks a new era. He added that watering green lawns every day is no longer possible.

London (CNN) – Voters in the UK have little time left to decide who they want to support, as polling stations open across the country in a fast-moving election. This campaign has been very short, especially compared to U.S. elections, where candidates often spend years preparing. The result could mean a change in government, with David Cameron’s Conservative Party possibly losing power to the Labour Party, led by Ed Miliband. Or, it could lead to a complicated process where party leaders try to form deals with smaller parties. But all that will only be known after the polls close late Thursday evening, local time.

This time of year, Christians around the world—over 2 billion people—think about the crucifixion and resurrection of Jesus. Because of the terrible attack on Christian college students in Kenya on Thursday, and the continuing danger faced by Christians in other countries, this Holy Week we are asking Christians to also remember how hundreds of thousands of Christians—and others—have been killed, tortured, enslaved, abused, or forced to flee their homes just because of their faith. Many have been crucified, beheaded, stoned, or bombed by religious extremists.

Three Ferguson, Missouri, city employees — including a police captain and a sergeant — were forced to resign or were fired after racist and offensive emails they sent were made public. The emails were found during a U.S. Justice Department investigation into racism in Ferguson’s police and court systems. The messages contained hateful remarks about President Barack Obama, First Lady Michelle Obama, Muslims, and other minorities. The Washington Post obtained the emails through a public records request on Thursday. CNN looked at the emails on Friday. The employees involved were Police Captain Rick Henke and Sergeant [last name not provided].

Two people, including a licensed greyhound trainer, have been arrested in Australia after at least 55 dog bodies were found dumped in the bush in Queensland, according to Australian media. The two suspects are from Bundaberg — a 71-year-old man and a 64-year-old woman. Both were charged with unlawfully having a firearm. The woman, who is a licensed greyhound trainer, was also charged with blocking police. Michael Beatty, a spokesman for RSPCA Queensland, said the investigation is still ongoing. RSPCA Queensland is helping Queensland police with the case.

Two years ago, Mike Premeau and Kathy Danke started a small business called Memories Gourmet Pizza Co. in their Wisconsin town. They sold frozen pizzas, including breakfast and gluten-free options, in stores across Nichols, which is west of Green Bay. They built a loyal customer base. But this week, their business was at risk because people confused them with Memories Pizza in Walkerton, Indiana. That restaurant made national news when its owners said they would not cater a same-sex wedding. As a result, angry people posted comments on Memories Gourmet Pizza’s Facebook page and called the business to protest.

Archaeologists in Austria found the complete skeleton of a camel under a cellar. The discovery was made during a dig in Tulln between 2006 and 2007, while looking for a shopping center. The team was from the University of Veterinary Medicine Vienna (Vetmeduni). Initially, experts thought the animal might have been a large horse or cow. But after looking at the neck bones, lower jaw, and forearm bones, archaeozoologist Alfred Galik said it was clearly a camel. This camel may have been used by Ottoman troops during their 17th-century siege of Vienna.

Andrew Getty, the 4-year-old grandson of J. Paul Getty, died Tuesday afternoon at his home in Los Angeles. His parents, Ann and Gordon Getty, said in a statement that they are asking the media and the public to respect their privacy during this hard time. The Los Angeles County coroner's office said the death "appears to be from natural causes or an accident." An officer, Ed Winter, said some medication was found at Getty's home, but it is not clear if Getty was taking it or what his medical history was.

We may never fully understand why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz crashed Germanwings Flight 9524 into the French Alps on March 24, killing everyone on board. The latest report shows he intentionally sped up the plane’s descent. It’s a shocking and terrifying event. As the investigation continues, we’ll learn more about how much he hid his mental illness, whether he asked for help, and how his depression affected his ability to fly. We’ll also have to ask if he should have stopped flying, and if his doctors should have warned someone. His case brings up big and important questions about people with mental illness and the shame and fear that often come with it.

April 8, 2015. After a news report about the U.S. and Cuba, CNN Student News looked at California’s serious drought. The drought is causing problems that could affect the whole country. There was a flu outbreak in Chicago, but it was in animals, not people. A plan was announced to build a tunnel under the sea connecting Denmark and Germany, with roads and train tracks inside. (CNN) He didn't give his real name. But the name "Gertrude" tattooed on his neck gave him away. That's what Kankakee County, Illinois, Sheriff Tim Bukowski said on Saturday about Kamron Taylor, a 33-year-old man who was convicted of murder and later escaped from jail. He was caught overnight in Chicago. Authorities across Illinois had been searching for Taylor since early Wednesday. He escaped after jumping a correctional officer at the Kankakee County Jerome Combs Detention Center, then stole the officer's uniform and an SUV. The last time officials saw Taylor was on surveillance video, just before midnight on Friday, in Chicago. "They saw a man who matched the description," Bukowski said.

As his military career comes to an end, Prince Harry is going to Australia. He is 30 years old and will arrive on Monday. He will spend four weeks there with the Australian Army. He will work and live with soldiers in regiments in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth. The Australian Defence Forces said this on Thursday. Harry has already spent time with Australian troops several times during his 10-year military career, a spokesman said.

Two Florida prison guards and a former trainee have been charged with planning to kill a former inmate. They used to guard prisons, but now they are the ones in jail. The Florida Attorney General's office said the men were involved in a plot to kill the former inmate, who was about to be released. An FBI informant, who had secretly joined a branch of the KKK called the Traditional American Knights of the Ku Klux Klan, met with the three men. According to court documents, Thomas Jordan Driver, 25, told the informant he had a fight with the inmate and that he and David Elliot Moran, 47, wanted the man dead. "six feet under" means they wanted him buried.

Lausanne, Switzerland (CNN) – A group of world powers, called the P5+1, reached a framework deal with Iran on its nuclear program. The deal still needs to be tested to see if it will work. The countries have until the end of June to finish the details and write the full agreement. The talks were a big moment, especially for the U States and Iran, which have not had good relations for a long time. But the talks were not flashy. Instead, they showed how diplomacy can be effective, but also very fast-paced and stressful.

An improvised bomb exploded near a U.N. vehicle traveling near Garowe, a city in northeastern Somalia, on Monday morning. Six people were killed, including four aid workers from UNICEF. Somalia’s president said the attack was an attack on the country’s future. This happened after another incident on Sunday, when three African Union soldiers died in an ambush in the Lower Shabelle region of Somalia. The terrorist group Al-Shabaab said it carried out Monday’s attack. The explosion happened around 8 a.m. in the administrative capital of the Puntland region, according to the United Nations Assistance Mission in Somalia.

Prince Harry arrived in Australia on Monday. He is 30 years old. Before starting his duties, he visited the Australian War Memorial in Canberra, the capital city. He paid his respects at the Tomb of the Unknown Australian Soldier. Many people were outside the memorial. Some took pictures of him, and one boy held a sign that said, "Red Heads Rule!" because of Harry's red hair. During his four-week stay, Harry will live and work with soldiers in the Australian Army. He will be with different army units in Sydney, Darwin, and Perth. This was announced by the Australian Defence Forces last week.

Australia, a key ally of the United States, has agreed to share some of its intelligence with Iran. Australian Foreign Minister Julie Bishop said the agreement is informal and mainly focuses on monitoring Australians who travel to Iraq to fight with ISIS. One Australian politician called the move "dancing with the devil." Bishop became the first Australian minister to visit Iran in two years over the weekend. She met with Iranian President Hassan Rouhani in Tehran. The intelligence-sharing deal was announced in an interview Bishop gave to the Australian Broadcasting Corporation while in Iran.

Marseille, France (CNN) – Initial tests on the flight data recorder from Germanwings Flight 9525 show that co-pilot Andreas Lubitz intentionally caused the plane to descend rapidly. This information comes from the French air accident investigation agency, the BEA. The flight data recorder, also known as the "black box," was found on Thursday by recovery teams who had searched for days in the French Alps since the crash on March 24. On Friday, the BEA released a statement saying their teams started examining the data right away.

CNN reported that a 110-day chase from Antarctic waters to west Africa ended unexpectedly when the crew of a suspected illegal fishing vessel, the Thunder, were rescued by conservation group Sea Shepherd. who had been chasing them. Sea Shepherd had been tracking the Thunder since it was first spotted by their ship, the Bob Barker, in the Southern Ocean several months earlier. The Thunder was listed by Interpol as a suspect in fraud and fishing crimes. The chase ended early Monday in the Gulf of Guinea, off west Africa, after the Bob Barker received a distress call from the Thunder.

Most days, 16-year-old Jason Zobott arrives at Huntley High School in suburban Chicago around 7:30 a.m., like most high school students. What he does after that is different. Zobott is in Huntley High’s blended learning program, which combines online lessons with regular classroom time. One-third of the school’s 2700 students are in the program. Garissa, Kenya (CNN) – After a deadly Al-Shabaab attack on Garissa University College that killed almost 50 people, Kenya carried out airstrikes against the group in Somalia. A military source said the strikes were not revenge for the Garissa attack. The source said the military operations against Al-Shabaab bases in Somalia began in 2011 and are still ongoing. The source added that these actions are part of a continuous effort, not a reaction to the recent massacre. Military sources in Kenya usually do not give their names to the media.

Pope Francis reminded the world that the Vatican is a country and that he serves as a moral leader during his Easter message. He spoke about the suffering caused by ongoing wars, especially in Iraq and Syria. He asked that the fighting stop and that people in need receive help. He urged the global community not to ignore the serious humanitarian crisis in these countries or the struggles of the many refugees. He made this message in his "urbi et orbi" speech, which means "to the city (Rome) and to the world."

CNN reported that Duke University students and faculty marched Wednesday afternoon, shouting "We are not afraid. We stand together," after a noose was found hanging from a tree on campus. The noose was discovered near a student center at 2 a.m. Duke officials are asking anyone with information to contact campus police. Photos of the noose spread quickly on social media, causing anger in the community. Later, hundreds of people gathered at a forum on the steps of Duke Chapel, close to where the noose was found. At the event, someone said, "You came here for the reason that you want to say with me, 'This is no Duke we will accept. This is no Duke we want. This is not the Duke we're here to experience."

A U.S. citizen, Muhanad Mahmoud Al Farekh, 29, did not enter a plea during his first court appearance on Thursday. He was deported from Pakistan to the U.S. He is accused of planning to fight against U.S. forces abroad. The charges were filed in a complaint unsealed in U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York in Brooklyn. CNN counterterrorism analyst Philip Mudd said this news is something to celebrate.

A Saudi border guard was killed in a fight with militants along the border between Saudi Arabia and Yemen this week, according to the Saudi Press Agency (SPA). This is the first time Saudi Arabia has publicly reported a military death since it started airstrikes against rebels in Yemen. The incident happened Wednesday night in the Asir region in southwestern Saudi Arabia. Militants in a mountainous area of Yemen fired on Saudi border troops, who returned fire. The dead guard was identified as Corporal Salman Ali Yahya al-Maliki. Ten other soldiers were injured, but their injuries were not serious.

Dubai (CNN) I felt a little nervous starting the Al Marmoum camel race in Dubai. As the only Gulf national on the CNN team, I was expected to know about camel racing — a long-standing tradition here. But even though I tried wearing a kandora, the UAE national dress, my modern way of life makes me feel like a stranger in this world. A friendly farm owner took us into the majlis — a special meeting area — where camel owners were gathering. The room was big and beautifully decorated, like a fancy theater. The camel owners were sitting on the floor, eating a traditional Arabic meal of fish and rice. The room was full of loud, excited talk.

Havana, Cuba — Charlie Hill is sitting in a dark bar on a very sunny day in Havana. "Hey, man," he says, his voice rough from smoking, nodding like he knows you’ve been looking for him. But a lot of people have been looking for him for a long time. For the past 43 years, Cuba has given Hill shelter from charges that he killed a New Mexico police officer and hijacked an airplane to Havana. Hill is now 65. After two years of trying to contact him, CNN finally got an interview. He says he’s now thinking about leaving Cuba and going back to the United States.

We also talk about where April Fools' Day comes from, share a 1000-year-old recipe that might help fight a dangerous modern infection, and tell the story of a woman who is helping kids build better lives. Misao Okawa, who was listed in Guinness World Records as the oldest person in the world, has died at the age of 117. She passed away on Wednesday morning in Osaka, Japan, according to Tadahi Uchimura, a local official. She had three children, four grandchildren, and six great grandchildren. Okawa was born on March 5, 1898. Her family owned a kimono shop in Osaka. Satoshi Yoshioka, an employee at the nursing home where she lived since 1997, said she was a quiet person who enjoyed eating. Her favorite foods were sushi and uhon noodles. She had eaten a lot of cake for her birthday in March 2023.

Washington (CNN) – When the Missouri National Guard was sent to Ferguson, Missouri, to help stop riots last year, they used strong military language like "enemy forces" and "adversaries" to describe the protesters, according to documents CNN obtained. The guard was sent to help local police, who many community leaders and civil rights groups said used too much force and made the tense situation worse. Protests happened off and on from August until the end of the year.

Mogadishu, Somalia (CNN) – Gunmen attacked the headquarters of Somalia's education ministry in the capital on Tuesday. The attack started with a suicide car bomb at the building's entrance. At least 12 people were killed and 16 others were injured, officials said. The Islamist group Al-Shabaab claimed responsibility. Their spokesman, Abu Musab, said the group carried out the attack. Two suicide bombers drove cars into the two-story building, which houses the Ministry of Education, Culture, and Higher Education. After the explosions, five gunmen entered the building and started shooting people inside, according to Somali National Security Ministry spokesman Mohamed Yusuf.

Gregory Margolin is now 87 years old. When he was 16, he joined the Soviet Red Army and fought against the Nazis in World War II. His family had to flee during the war. He says he didn't show he was Jewish, but it didn't matter—people were dying all around him. This year, in Ukraine, he found himself in another war. He had once been a sniper and later became a commander. His old military uniform still has the medals he earned. His granddaughter, Liora, still listens to his war stories with awe. She can't believe he lived through it all.

More than 200 Nigerian schoolgirls vanished. It happened in Chibok, in northeastern Nigeria, in the middle of the night. It has now been 365 days since they were taken. The girls are still missing. This should make us all feel ashamed. We should be ashamed that in our world, young girls can be taken by violent extremists without anyone stopping them. We should also feel ashamed that people quickly stop paying attention to such terrible events.

CNN. Video may have killed the radio star, but in Norway, it's digital that's replacing FM radio. In two years, Norway will be the first country in the world to completely stop using FM radio. That doesn't mean people will have no radio at all—they’ll just have to listen using digital technology. In Oslo, officials say most people in this country of 5 million already use digital radio. Right now, only five radio stations are available on FM. On the digital radio network, there are four times as many—20 stations. Half of Norway already listens to radio through digital, said Culture Minister Thorhild Widvey.

CNN says everyone loves a good comeback story — especially one that's as big as a dinosaur. A new study shows that the Brontosaurus should be recognized as its own type of dinosaur, not just a version of the Apatosaurus. This means it deserves to keep its own name. In 1879, O.C. Marsh named the Brontosaurus after he got 25 crates of bones from a dig site at Como Bluff in Wyoming, according to the Yale Peabody Museum of Natural History.. The dinosaur was named "Brontosaurus," which means " thunder lizard." The Brontosaurus was similar to but smaller than the Apatosaurus, which had been found a few years earlier.

Al Qaeda in Yemen, known as AQAP, has a new online video and poster, saying it is offering 20 kilograms of gold, to anyone who kills or captures two major Shia Muslim leaders. These include the head of the Houthi rebels, Abdelmalik Bedrudin Al-Houthi, and former Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh. The gold is worth about $774,000 in money. AQAP called both men "the two heads of evil." AQAP is one of many groups fighting for control of Yemen.

Before landing his gyrocopter on the Capitol lawn on Wednesday, Doug Hughes, a 61-year-old Florida postal worker, posted on a website called thedemocracyclub.org. He said he wanted to draw attention to corruption in Washington, D.C., and also to offer solutions to the problem. He said his flight was not a surprise. He had emailed Barack Obama’s office at info@barackobama.com before taking off. In the email, he tried to convince Capitol officials that he wasn’t a threat. He said shooting him down would cause more trouble than just letting him deliver his letters to Congress.

The bad news for Rio de Janeiro keeps growing. After many dead fish were found in the Rodrigo de Freitas lagoon, officials from Rio's state legislature started an investigation on Monday. They want to find out why the fish died. This happened in the lagoon and in other lakes and bays across the state. The investigation will be done with help from the State Environmental Institute (INEA) and the State Secretariat for the Environment. The Olympics are less than a year away, and Rio is set to host rowing and canoe events there.

Anthony Ray Hinton is 58 years old. But in many ways, he is just starting to experience life — especially the everyday things most people take for granted. Things like using a fork, going out at night, or going to bed without someone watching over you. These are all new for Hinton, who spent almost 30 years on Alabama's death row. Just a week ago, his murder convictions were overturned, and he finally left the county jail in Birmingham. "I have to pinch myself to believe I’m really free," he told CNN’s Brooke Baldwin. "It will take time, but I’ll get used to it." For 30 years, Hinton spent most of his time locked in a small 5-by-7 cell.

The opinion polls after the UK election debate showed no clear winner. The seven party leaders were David Cameron (Conservatives), Ed Miliband (Labour), Nick Clegg (Liberal Democrats), Nigel Farage (UKIP), Natalie Bennett (Green Party), Nicola Sturgeon (SNP), and Leanne Wood (Plaid Cymru). 

Polls from Comres for ITV showed Cameron, Miliband, and Farage tied for first with 21% each, and Sturgeon close behind with 20%. Another poll by ICM for The Guardian gave Miliband 25%, Cameron 24%, Farage 19%, and Sturgeon 17%.

CNN reports that Facebook might soon include "Just got served divorce papers" as a relationship status. A New York judge has ruled that sending divorce papers through Facebook is a valid way to serve them. The case involves Ellanora Arthur Baidoo, a Brooklyn woman trying to divorce her husband, Victor Sena Blood-Dzraku. Her lawyer, Andrew Spinnell, said they’ve struggled for years to serve him the divorce papers. Baidoo has tried calling her husband, but he told her he has no fixed address and no job. Court documents confirm this.

It sounds like a scene from a sci-fi movie. Someone has a terrible accident and is left brain dead, on life support. Doctors talk to the family about donating organs, but instead of saving up to eight people, they’re asked to donate the whole body to save just one person—maybe someone who is paralyzed but has a sharp mind. Even though it sounds impossible, Italian doctor Sergio Canavero says we are getting close to doing something called HEAVEN. That’s short for Head Anastomosis Venture. "Anastomosis" means joining two parts together surgically. He believes it might soon be possible to transplant a human head onto a new body.

Anthony Stokes was supposed to have a happy ending after getting a heart transplant. Instead, on Tuesday, police said he carjacked someone, broke into a home, shot at an elderly woman, led police on a high-speed chase, and died when his car hit a pole. In 2013, his family said an Atlanta hospital turned him down for a heart transplant because he had a history of not following medical advice, according to a letter from the hospital. At the time, Mark Bell was speaking for the Stokes family.

The sun had not risen at Garissa University College. Most students were still asleep in their beds. A few had woken up to go to early morning Christian prayers. Then the attack started. There was an explosion and gunshots around 5 a.m. on Thursday (1030 p.m. ET Wednesday) at the school’s front gates. The attackers kept shooting as they moved through the campus. The Red Cross said they stopped at a dormitory for girls. At one point, they broke into a room where Christians were praying and took people hostage, said lecturer Joel Ayora.

A white casket was at the front of New Shiloh Baptist Church in West Baltimore while a gospel choir sang for a large crowd. The crowd had come to honor Freddie Gray, a 25-year-old man who died 15 days earlier while in police custody. He was arrested on a weapons charge. He died from a serious spinal cord injury. His death caused anger toward the Baltimore Police Department. His death is part of a growing number of high-profile cases involving Black people and police. Many people are asking what really happened to Gray. His funeral was attended by civil rights leaders, politicians, and family members of others who died in police custody.

I’ve been working in food since I was 14. But I didn’t become a food activist until 2007, when my wife’s mentee was found digging through trash looking for food. That moment changed me. I started Food Policy Action and got involved in food issues like hunger and factory farming. I wasn’t alone— a big turning point was "The Meatrix," a 2003 video parody of "The Matrix" made by the GRACE Communications Foundation. It clearly showed how factory farming harms public health and the environment.

CNN's Dan Swangard knows what death looks like. As a doctor, he has seen patients die in hospitals, suffering and hooked to morphine. He has watched people struggle to the end for weeks or months, while family members could do nothing. Recently, though, his thoughts about dying have become personal. In 2013, he was diagnosed with a rare type of cancer that has spread. To treat it, doctors removed parts of his pancre and liver, as well as his entire spleen and gallbladder. The surgery worked, but Swangard, who is 48, knows he likely will get sick again.

CNN reported that Saudi special forces helped Yemeni fighters fight against the Houthis and their allies in Aden. The Saudi forces were on the ground in non-combat roles, helping to coordinate and direct the fighting. They also assisted in dropping weapons and communication equipment by parachute. The Houthis later pulled back from the presidential palace and other important areas in Aden after intense Saudi airstrikes. This retreat came after the Houthis had captured the presidential palace just the day before.

A Detroit mother was arrested last month after police found the bodies of two of her children in a freezer. She was formally charged this week with murder and torture. Wayne County Prosecutor Kym Worthy said the mother, Mitchelle Angela Blair, is accused of killing her 13-year-old daughter, Stoni Ann Blair, and her 9-year-old son, Stephen Gage Berry. The bodies were discovered on March 24 by a bailiff carrying out a court-ordered eviction. Detroit Police Chief James Craig said the bodies were wrapped in plastic and found inside the freezer. The Wayne County medical examiner later ruled that Stoni died from multiple blunt force injuries, and Stephen died from multiple blunt force injuries and burns.

Wladimir Klitschko, the world heavyweight boxing champion, has an important fight coming up on April 25 against American boxer Bryant Jennings in New York. But right now, his mind is mostly on the fight for democracy in Ukraine. He spoke to CNN from his training base in Miami. He said the war in Ukraine has deeply upset him. "My country is suffering because of the war with Russia," he said. "Ukraine did not start the fighting. Russia is the one that attacked."

Michael Keaton hosted "Saturday Night Live" for the third time this weekend. He made a small joke about his past roles in "Beetlejuice" and "Batman" during his opening monologue. He said it's been a long time since he first hosted in 1982, and he now has a 31-year-old son and a 28-year-old girlfriend. Fans who hoped to see him fully play Batman or Beetlejuice were not disappointed by a full revival. Instead, when cast members Taran Killam and Bobby Moynihan sang a request for him to play those characters, he only gave a few short jokes in return.

When he did, he attacked a jail guard who was on duty. Taylor hit the officer, put on the guard’s uniform and took his keys. A New York City detective has been suspended after being accused of stealing $3,000 during a raid on an illegal cigarette operation. Police spokesman Stephen Davis said the incident happened last Friday at the Yemen Deli and Grocery store in Brooklyn. Surveillance video from a CNN affiliate, News 12 Brooklyn, shows Detective Ian Cyrus putting cash into a bag before leaving the store. The detectives had arrested two store employees for selling loose cigarettes. The store’s manager, Ali Abdullah, noticed the money was missing from a box. At first, he thought one of his employees took it. But when he checked the security cameras, he was shocked by what he saw.

London (CNN) – A major robbery at a well-known London safe deposit company over the holiday weekend has become known as the Hatton Garden heist. Thieves used powerful cutting tools and rappelling gear to break into the company’s vault. The company is 60 years old and located in central London. The thieves may have had up to four days to search through the uncounted number of safe deposit boxes. They are believed to have stolen gems and cash worth hundreds of thousands of pounds. One former police officer estimates they may have taken as much as 200 million pounds (or $300 million).

On April 2, South Africa will mark the anniversary of its first post-apartheid elections in 1994. At the same time, the country is dealing with another wave of violent attacks against African migrants. People are angry and speaking out on social media, using the hashtag #WeAreAfrica to show unity and demand action. These repeated attacks on migrants and their belongings suggest that South Africa’s dream of a united, diverse nation may be failing. That dream was about a country where people of all races and backgrounds could live with dignity.

In 1989, Ayatollah Khomeini said he was "drinking poison" when he agreed to a ceasefire that ended the eight-year war with Iraq. The war had played a big role in shaping Khomeini's regime, the Islamic Republic, which he had created just a year before Saddam Hussein invaded Iran. Khomeini inspired both his supporters and growing critics to fight against Iraq. He kept the war going for eight years, even though Saddam had offered a ceasefire. This helped strengthen the Islamic Republic. But by the time the war ended, the economy was destroyed, and Khomeini’s most loyal fighters were gone.

CNN says that the idea of sustainable development comes from the fact that raw capitalism is too powerful and harmful to itself. The global economy is growing very fast—doubling in size every generation. But Earth has limited resources, and every 15 years, about 1 billion new people are added. This rapid growth is now damaging the natural world and the social systems that help people live good, decent lives. Sustainable development is a way to solve this worsening crisis. The truth is that raw capitalism is based on greed.

The United States has benefited greatly from being a space-faring nation. Space has helped keep the country safe, supported its military, and boosted its economy. To handle today’s and future threats, including war, terrorism, and growing global dangers, the U.S. military depends on space systems like spy satellites, GPS, and communication satellites. But there's a serious problem: as threats grow and the need for reliable access to space gets stronger, the U.S. still depends too much on Russian technology to carry out its national security duties.

On the one-year anniversary of when nearly 300 schoolgirls were kidnapped by Boko Haram in Nigeria, Malala Yousafzai sent an open letter to the girls. She wrote, "I was also targeted by militants who didn't want girls to go to school." She is a 17-year-old Nobel Peace Prize winner who survived a Taliban attack in Pakistan. The Taliban had attacked her because she wrote online about the importance of girls going to school. In her letter, she asks the Nigerian government and the world to do more to rescue the girls. Nigeria recently held an election.

Johannesburg (CNN) – South African troops were sent in on Tuesday evening as part of a new government plan to stop deadly violence against immigrants. Their first stop was the Johannesburg suburb of Jeppestown, where the violence started on Friday. Police raided a hostel in Jeppestown on Tuesday while troops guarded the area. Earlier, Defense Minister Nosiviwe Mapisa-Nqakula said the government would send an unknown number of troops to places where police are too stretched to stop attacks on immigrants. "This intervention is not an indictment on the police."

Eight Iranian border guards were killed in fights with armed militants near the border with Pakistan, Iranian state media said. Three of the militants were killed by Iranian forces during the clashes on Monday in the town of Negur, according to the state news agency IRNA. The agency quoted Ali Asghar Mirshekari, the deputy governor of Iran's Sistan-Baluchestan province, saying the militants had crossed into Iran from Pakistan. Iranian officials have asked Pakistani authorities to catch the remaining attackers.

CNN. If you love island-hopping, take note: Providenciales in the Turks and Caicos has been named the best island in the world by TripAdvisor. It moved up one spot from last year’s second place to take the top spot, pushing Ambergris Caye in Belize out of first. Ambergris Caye had been number one for two years in a row, but this year it dropped out of the top 10 entirely. TripAdvisor spokeswoman Julie Cassetina said it's hard to say why the change happened, but rankings change each year based on traveler feedback.

The "Star Wars" universe is growing. At the Star Wars Celebration fan festival in Anaheim, California, on Sunday, details about the 2016 movie "Star Wars: Rogue One" were shared. Director Gareth Edwards, who also made "Godzilla," showed a short teaser for the film. He also revealed the plot. The movie is part of the "Star Wars" anthology series — what Disney calls the "spinoff" films. Felicity Jones stars in the movie. The story takes place between "Episode III: Revenge of the Sith" and "Episode IV: A New Hope" — the first "Star Wars" movie from 1977. A group of rebels takes a secret mission to steal the plans for the Death Star. Felicity Jones plays a rebel

Tehran, Iran (CNN) – There is a Persian saying: "A good year starts with a good spring." Many Iranians believe that the recent decision by Tehran and six major countries — the U.S., UK, France, Germany, Russia, and China — to keep negotiating on Iran’s nuclear program under a "joint comprehensive plan of action" is a sign that this year’s Norouz, the Persian New Year that began on March 2, will be a good one. Even though some tough conservative voices may complain that the agreement isn’t exactly what they wanted, most people see it as real progress — and that’s what they care about.

One Israeli man was killed and another was injured in what police believe was a suspected terror attack Wednesday night near Hebrew University in Jerusalem. A 37-year-old Arab man from East Jerusalem drove into two people waiting at a bus stop in the French Hill area. The victim, Shalom Yohai Cherki, 26, died at the hospital. A 20-year-old woman is still in serious condition. The driver has been arrested and is being questioned by Israel’s General Security Services.

An art collection owned by the late Hollywood star Lauren Bacall has been put up for sale. The collection, which includes pieces by major 20th-century artists, was auctioned in New York on March 31. It had previously been shown in Hong Kong, Paris, London, and Los Angeles. Bacall, who died in August 2014 at age 89, first became famous in 1944 with her film debut in "To Have and Have Not." was also when she met her future husband, Humphrey Bogart. In his 2015 Golden Globe acceptance speech, George Clooney honored Bacall.

Kiev, Ukraine (CNN) – People in Kiev are asking: Who is killing people who were close to Ukraine’s former President Viktor Yanukovych? This question isn't completely new. But it came back into focus this week after two high-profile killings in the capital. One was a former lawmaker linked to Yanukovych. The other was a Ukrainian journalist known for supporting Russia. Oleg Kalashnikov, the former lawmaker, was shot and killed just after 7 p.m. on Wednesday at the entrance of his apartment building.

Same-sex civil unions will soon be recognized in Chile. President Michelle Bachelet signed a new law on Monday that gives legal rights to couples living together, whether they are two men, two women, or a man and a woman. The law will go into effect in six months. Bachelet said this is an important step toward treating gay and straight couples equally. The Chilean government says about 2 million people will benefit from this new law.

When you fly to visit Grandma in Florida, look down. When you take the kids to see the talking mouse or go to South Beach for sun and fun, sit by the window and think about what you're seeing as you land. Below you is the Everglades — a huge, wet, swampy area full of dangerous animals like snakes, scorpions, rats, roaches, alligators, and mosquitoes. One scientist once caught 650,00 bloodthirsty mosquitoes in just one trap in one night. This place shows how people have made big mistakes trying to change nature, and how hard it is to fix those mistakes.

CNN reported that ISIS fighters took over Yarmouk, a Palestinian refugee camp near Damascus. For over two years, the people of Yarmouk had been under siege and bombing by Syrian forces. In early April, they woke up to a new and even worse situation — ISIS had taken control of most of the camp after defeating several local militia groups. One resident, who did not want to be named, told CNN that ISIS fighters killed people in the streets. He said they caught three people and killed them right in front of others. Now, ISIS controls almost all of Yarmouk.

China's internet censors have long used the "Great Firewall" to block Chinese people from reading critical articles from Western news sites or viewing other content they don't approve of.. But now, according to a study released on Friday, they have created a new tool. They've used it to attack servers outside China, including in the United States. The researchers who wrote the study call this new tool the "Great Cannon." It works openly, right in the view of others. The study says that attacking servers in another country so openly and easily is likely to upset other nations. But the researchers think Beijing may have expected this reaction and planned for it.

The investigation into the crash of Germanwings Flight 9525 has not found any proof of why co-pilot Andreas Lubitz crashed the plane. But a spokesman for the prosecutor's office in Dusseldorf, Germany, said Lubitz had shown signs of suicidal thoughts at some point before he became a pilot. Investigators have not found any notes, messages, or talks where Lubitz explained his reasons or said he planned to do this. The spokesman, Christoph Kumpa, said medical records show Lubitz was suicidal in the past and had received therapy. This happened before he ever got his pilot's license.

The leader of Yemen's Houthi rebels said on Sunday that his fighters would not leave major cities or government buildings, calling any idea that they would give up a fantasy.. This came after more than three weeks of airstrikes by a Saudi-led coalition. The strikes were meant to stop the Houthis, who took over the capital, Sanaa, in January and forced President Abdu Rabu Mansour Hadi to flee.

On April 19, 1995, Timothy McVeigh set off a large truck bomb in front of the Murrah Federal Building in Oklahoma City. The explosion killed 168 people—men, women, and children—and and hundreds more were injured. It is the deadliest act of domestic terrorism in U.S. history. The bombing shocked the nation. The media widely covered it, with messages like "attack on the heartland" and America's "lost innocence." The bombing surprised the country. It wasn’t just the size of the tragedy that made people pay attention. It was also new that an American had attacked their own government with such deadly force—something that had never happened before.

If you really cared about something, would you protest? Would you make a sign? Join a march? How long could you keep going, even if no one listened or did anything? A year ago, more than 200 Nigerian girls were taken from their school by Boko Haram fighters. Millions of people worldwide joined a social media campaign to demand their safe return. Charles Alasholuyi was one of them — from famous people to world leaders — all speaking out against the kidnapping using the hashtag #BringBackOurGirls. This hashtag was one of the most used on Twitter in 20000, appearing in over four million tweets. But as weeks turned into months, and still no girls came back, the attention on the campaign slowly disappeared.

Barney Frank, who has a lot of experience in politics, recently spoke in Chicago to a full crowd at the Center on Halsted. He talked about his four years in public service. Frank was the first member of Congress to get married to someone of the same sex while still in office. He also strongly criticized politicians who hide their sexuality and vote against LGBT rights. When someone in the audience asked about a California ballot measure that would allow killing gay people, Frank said he didn’t know about the proposal. He told the young person not to worry about "the crazy people."

A violent attack on Garissa University College in Kenya has killed almost 50 people, including students, and left many others injured. Gunmen stormed the campus early Thursday during morning prayers, opening fire randomly and taking hostages before being killed by security forces. The U.S. Embassy in Nairobi said Al-Shabaab is responsible. This attack follows a similar incident months earlier, when Al-Shabaab killed non-Muslim workers at a quarry in Kenya. The group has carried out many attacks in the region and has also recruited some Americans, especially from the Somali-American community in Minnesota.

A South African university is celebrating the removal of a statue of British colonialist Cecil Rhodes. Students at the University of Cape Town used social media to demand the statue be taken down, saying Rhodes' legacy is linked to racism. They started a campaign using the hashtag #RhodesMustFall. The campaign began last month. Four weeks later, the hashtag changed to #RhodesHasFallen. The university said it received permission from the heritage authority to remove the statue. It added that the move is to keep the statue safe while decisions are made about its future.

CNN says Syria is like hell and is getting worse. The number of people killed there has doubled in one year, according to an opposition group. Since the civil war started, 310000 people have died, according to the Syrian Observatory for Human Rights (SOHR). A year ago, SOHR reported 162,402 deaths. Two years ago, the United Nations said about 70,000 had died. The UN also says that more than half of all Syrians are now in terrible poverty and need help to survive. This is because food aid is being reduced due to lack of donations.

(Ailina Tsarnaeva walked into Manhattan Criminal Court quietly and appeared shy. But prosecutors say she was not afraid to threaten a woman. In a phone call this summer, she told the woman, "Leave my man alone. Stop looking for him." She also said, "I know people that can put a bomb where you live," according to a criminal complaint. Because of who she is — the sister of Dzhokhar and Tamerlan Tsarnaev — prosecutors took the threat seriously. They charged her with aggravated harassment, which she denies. Last December, after leaving court, she and her lawyer refused to talk about the case.

A door painted with graffiti by British artist Banksy was taken by police in Gaza on Thursday after a dispute over its sale, a Gaza police official told CNN. The door’s owner, Rabea Darduna, said he didn’t know how valuable it was when he sold it for $175 U.S. He filed a complaint with a Gaza court. The iron door is now being held by the Khan Younis police in southern Gaza. The court will decide when to hold a hearing, but the date is not yet known. Darduna said his home in Gaza was destroyed during last summer’s war. He said he felt he had nothing left—only a doorway and a door.

CNN reported that the fighting against the Houthis rebels in Yemen continued on Tuesday. The Saudi-led coalition said it was gaining more control, but many locals were fleeing because of the violence. Dozens of civilians were killed or injured. Five days after the first airstrikes, the coalition had destroyed most of the Houthis' and their allies' air defense systems. Most air bases and runways were now unusable, according to a Saudi source. Saudi Arabia's navy now controls all Yemeni ports. Only non-military medical supplies are allowed through the blockade, and they are closely monitored.

Holland's manager Guus Hiddink criticized his own fans for booing Spain's Andres Iniesta during Holland's 2-0 win over Spain. The match took place at the Amsterdam Arena. Spain played a young, experimental team, with Iniesta coming on in the 76th minute. He was greeted with loud jeers and boos from the home crowd. Holland's defenders Stefan de Vrij and Davy Klaassen scored in the first half to give Holland the win. But Hiddink said the way Iniesta was treated was shameful. He called the fans' behavior a 'disgrace'. Iniesta played for Spain in the match, which Holland won 2-0.

On May 21, Scotland will find out if their Euro 2016 qualifier against Georgia in September will be played without fans. UEFA has started a disciplinary case against the Georgian Football Federation (GFF) after fans ran onto the field twice during Georgia's 2-0 loss to Germany in Tbilisi on Sunday. UEFA will also investigate reports that home fans set off fireworks, and safety problems at the Boris Paichadze Stadium, including blocked stairs, locked gates, and staff not doing body searches. A fan ran onto the pitch during the match in Tbilisi.

On Wednesday, football agents were unsure what to expect while waiting for new rules. Starting April 1, anyone can become a football agent by paying £500 for a one-year registration. The FA will then charge £250 each year to keep the license. Existing licensed agents do not have to pay again. The FA was supposed to put a link on its website so intermedi players could register, but as of 1pm that link was still not there. Mel Stein believes the new rules will cause chaos. The changes came after FIFA stopped overseeing football agents.

Maksims Uvarenko, a Latvian goalkeeper for financially struggling CSKA Sofia, hasn't been paid in three months. He has had to ask his parents to send him money to cover his rent. Even though he's facing money problems, Uvarenko said he's been impressed by the club's fans and their strong support. He told local media that the lack of salary is his biggest issue since joining the Bulgarian club in January. He still hasn't received any pay after three months with the team. David Moore, 25, lost control and attacked another driver after leaving his home. He got stuck in heavy traffic and came face to face with Rafal Cegielka, 45, who was picking up his child from St John's Primary School in Burnley, Lancashire. The incident happened because Moore was having a bad day and became extremely angry. He punched Cegielka, then used a hockey stick to smash his car, all in front of young children. This was reported in court.

Spain lost 2-0 to Holland on Tuesday, reminding people of their poor performance at the 2014 World Cup. But defender Gerard Piqué says coach Vicente del Bosque shouldn’t be too worried about Spain’s third straight friendly loss. Holland scored two early goals at the Amsterdam Arena and managed to hold on despite strong pressure from Spain in the second half. This followed Holland’s 5-1 win over Spain in the group stage of the 2014 World Cup in Brazil, which ended Spain’s six-year dominance in world football.

A large fire burned through dry heathland near the south coast. Flames jumped high and thick smoke rose into the sky. The fire destroyed an area as big as 100 football fields. This happened after several days of storms had damaged parts of Britain, knocking down trees and closing roads. The 70-hectare area in Dorset was very dry because it is on a hillside and water had run off. Fire investigators said the fire was started on purpose. Three separate areas of heath were burned: one was half a hectare, one was one hectare, and one was 70 hectares.

Emergency services got 600 calls every hour last night as people across Britain celebrated the New Year. Paramedics were very busy, and in Cambridge, a field hospital from the Territorial Army was set up to help drunk partygoers. The London Ambulance Service said they had more than 600 calls per hour at the busiest time – that’s over three times more than on a normal night.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet said his mental strength helped him get through being dropped in December. He was left out of the team by manager Brendan Rodgers after a bad run of form, but came back quickly when Brad Jones got a thigh injury. The 27-year-old Belgian said he stayed positive even though he was upset about losing his place. Mignolet made a save from a free kick in a recent match against Swansea. He told FourFourTwo: "I was positive."

Large hailstones, about the size of plums, fell over the southern U.S. on Tuesday. People rushed outside to film the unusual weather. Arke USA, a Twitter user from Bryant, Arkansas, recorded the hail hitting his backyard and bouncing into his swimming pool. The video shows the hail falling fast, with many breaking apart when they hit the ground. Even though the temperature was around 80 degrees, the hard hailstones didn’t melt quickly. Within seconds, the patio was completely covered in white hail pellets.

A group of nine people on a replica pirate schooner called the Liana's Ransom had to leave their ship after it lost power in heavy seas off the coast of Maine.. The Coast Guard rescued them using life boats on Tuesday. The ship, which is from Canada, was left floating 30 miles east of Portland. The crew said their engines stopped working around 12:35 a.m. on Monday. They also said the sails had gotten caught around the mast. The Coast Guard confirmed the rescue.

Strange blue glowing algae have been seen along Australia’s east coast. The photos were taken in Jervis Bay, on the south coast of New South Wales. The glow came from millions of tiny plankton that give off light. Photographer Andy Hutchinson said it looked like a magical, otherworldly scene. A similar glowing effect was seen at Manly Beach in Sydney in August 20014. An oceanography expert said there was nothing to worry about with the algae.

A 17-year-old boy named Rahul Kumar was drunk when he climbed into the lion enclosure at the Kamla Nehru Zoological Park in Ahmedabad, India. He ran toward the lions, shouting he would kill them. Security had to rescue him. He said later that he was drunk and thought he could beat the lions. He had been sitting near the enclosure before suddenly running into it.

A 2-year-old boy in Nanchang, the capital of Jiangxi Province in southeastern China, survived after falling from a fifth-floor window. His father said the boy likely fell while sleepwalking. The incident happened last Saturday. The boy landed on a car parked below, which helped save his life. A hotel receptionist across the street said she heard a loud noise around midnight and thought it was a car crash.

Drew Miller of the Red Wings says he’s ready to play again just one day after getting a serious cut to his face that could have damaged his eyesight.. " I feel very lucky the skate didn’t hit my eye," Miller said at practice on Wednesday. He was wearing a full face mask while skating. The Detroit Free Press reports he had a deep, ugly wound that needed 5 to 6 stitches. The cut went through several layers of skin and left a scar across his eye. But he didn’t lose any eyesight, even though another player cut him during a game.

Filipe Luis says he wants to stay at Chelsea until his contract ends, even though Atletico Madrid is thinking about bringing him back in the summer. He signed a three-year deal when he moved from Atletico last July, but hasn’t been able to secure the left back spot at Chelsea. Atletico hopes this might help them get him back, but Luis said, “I’m happy at Chelsea. I want to stay at the club until the end of my contract.”

A Reading football fan, Charlie Sumner, 20, could get banned from football for three years after running onto the pitch topless during his first ever game at Madejski Stadium. The incident happened in the FA Cup quarter-final replay against Bradford City, when Reading were already leading 3-0. Sumner did four front somersaults on the pitch, landing on his back, before being stopped by stewards. He said watching his first game was a " brilliant experience," but now faces a possible three-year ban for the stunt.

A video has been released showing a dangerous moment when a van carrying several men on its roof flipped over while turning sharply on a road near Salé, Morocco. About six people were riding on top of the van when it suddenly tipped onto its side at high speed. The video, filmed from a car behind the van, shows the vehicle weaving back and forth on a busy road, likely a dual carriageway. The van is believed to have been carrying football fans. The footage captures the terrifying moment the men were thrown off the van as it rolled.

England have been placed in Group D of the UEFA Under-17 European Championships, which will be held in Bulgaria in May. The group also includes the Republic of Ireland, Holland, and Italy. England are the defending champions, having beaten Holland on penalties in last year’s final in Malta. To reach the quarter-finals, England will need to beat Holland again. This year’s tournament has expanded from eight to 16 teams for the first time. Danny Collinge celebrated by running away after scoring his first goal for England against Norway in the qualifying matches.

An angry elephant sprayed water from its trunk at a buffalo bull that got too close while the elephant was relaxing with its family at a small pool in Kruger National Park, South Africa. The elephant was trying to scare the bull away, but missed. The video shows the elephant trying again, clearly annoyed. The baby elephant stayed close to its mother for safety while the bull drank from the pool.

Michael Thorpe, a former pub landlord, has had his conviction overturned after eight years. He was convicted in November 2006 for showing a Premier League football match on a foreign TV channel at the Stoke Inn in Plymouth, Devon. At the time, he did not have a deal with the official broadcasters. Mr Thorpe, who is 55, says the long legal fight has cost him dearly. He lost his pub as a result of the case.

The Irish Football Association hopes that damage to its home stadium, Windsor Park in Belfast, won’t stop the team from playing its important Euro 2016 qualifier against Romania in June. Cracks were found in the West Stand on Tuesday morning, and the area was closed off while structural engineers checked the damage. An IFA spokesman said they learned about the damage on Tuesday morning, which happened during the night. The West Stand at Windsor Park, Northern Ireland’s home stadium, was damaged overnight on Monday.

A football fan is at risk of a three-year ban after running topless onto the pitch and doing several somersaults during his first ever game at the stadium.. Charlie Sumner, 20, broke onto the field at Reading's Madejski Stadium during the FA Cup quarter-final replay against Bradford City last month. He did four front flips on the grass, landing on his back each time, while Reading was leading 3-0. He was then taken down by stadium staff.

A man driving a BMW with five children in the car was arrested today after a young student, Hina Shamim, was hit and killed while walking to the library. The incident happened near the University of Kingston in London. Hina, who was two years old, died just weeks before her second birthday. She was from Peterborough and was known to friends as "Hyena." People who knew her said she was much loved and very special. Flowers have been left at the scene by her friends.

A mother and her teenage daughter were arrested after a video showed them fighting with a student at Langham Creek High School in Houston. The incident happened on Tuesday and was caught on camera. The mother, whose name hasn’t been released, was reportedly upset because she believed the student had been bullying her daughter. According to Channel 2, the mother was wearing a black top and was on the right in the video. The student who was attacked was in the center, wearing white.

Stoke chief executive Tony Scholes hopes the club can keep goalkeeper Asmir Begovic, who is in the final year of his contract. The Bosnia international has often been linked with other clubs since joining Stoke. Although his current deal ends in just over two months, Scholes believes Stoke can meet Begovic’s goals and ambitions. "Asmir is a top goalkeeper, and we really want him to stay," Scholes said. "It's normal for top players to attract interest and talk about their future."

A bus driver in Auckland, New Zealand, was strongly criticized by his boss after being caught on video reading a newspaper while driving. A passenger filmed the driver while the bus was moving and sent the video to the bus company, Ritchies Coachlines, with a complaint. In the video, the driver is seen turning the pages of a newspaper. At one point, the bus slows down at traffic lights, and the driver looks at a page. The company’s boss, Andrew Ritchie, said he was embarrassed by the driver’s actions and called him a "complete idiot."

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce has said Winston Reid will be fit for Saturday's game against Leicester City, who are at the bottom of the league. Reid had been out since he hurt his hamstring in a 1-0 loss to Chelsea on March 4. He returned to full training during the international break. However, Enner Valencia will not play. He missed West Ham's last two matches against Arsenal and Sunderland because of a strange toe injury he got at home in mid-March. Allardyce says Valencia is still not ready for match play. Reid, the West Ham defender, was seen earlier in February fighting with Tottenham's Mousa Dembele.

Five days before Brittany Huber and John Redman were supposed to get married last May, a terrible car crash on a Georgia highway killed Brittany and seriously injured John. Redman survived, but his body was badly broken. Doctors told him he would probably spend the rest of his life in a nursing home, in a wheelchair. At 25, Redman was an assistant basketball coach at Dalton State College, and his future seemed very dark. But he fought hard and made a strong recovery. On March 24, he helped lead his team to win a championship.

Lucas (on the left) was seen with Liverpool captain Steven Gerrard during Sunday’s All-Star charity game at Anfield. Liverpool midfielder Lucas Leiva is trying to get back to the form he had two years ago after recovering from injury. He had 16e starts in 19 games from late November, which matched a period when Liverpool’s results got much better. A groin injury in February’s Merseyside derby made him miss 10 games. He didn’t play in the loss to Manchester United just before the international break — that was the first league game since mid-December. But he played the full 90 minutes in Sunday’s charity game at Anfield.

Tired of boring father-daughter photos? One photographer has come up with a strange but effective way to make them more fun. Japanese photographer Yûki Aoyama's new photo series shows serious-looking teenagers standing next to their fathers, who are jumping in the air. In each photo, the daughter looks straight at the camera and smiles, while her father makes a dramatic pose. These photos are part of a new book by the 37-year-old photographer. The book’s title, which roughly means "Daughter and Salary Man," reflects the theme of the photos.

Police are looking for a man between 50 and 60 years old. He is 5ft 9in to 6ft tall and was wearing black clothes. He robbed a Lloyds Bank in Fairwater, Cardiff, at 12.30pm. He took £3,000 in cash. The suspect is a white man with greying black hair and glasses. He was seen on CCTV inside the bank. No one was hurt during the robbery. Police are confident the public can help identify him. They have shared CCTV images of the man.

The Court of Arbitration for Sport has removed Morocco's ban from the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments. Morocco was originally banned by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) after pulling out of hosting the 2017 and 2019 tournaments. CAF had expelled Morocco and fined it $1 million. CAF also asked for an additional $9 million in compensation, because Morocco withdrew due to fears about the Ebola epidemic. Morocco had been set to host the tournament, which was eventually won by Ivory Coast in Equatorial Guinea. Now, Morocco is allowed to take part in the next two African Cup of Nations tournaments after the ban was lifted.

Tom Boyd thinks Jason Denayer has done so well during his loan at Celtic that he is now ready to fight for a spot at Manchester City next season. This might go against Celtic manager Ronny Deila’s plan to keep Denayer for another year, but Boyd sees a good side to it. He believes Denayer’s progress can help attract more young players to join Celtic. The 19-year-old defender, Jason Denayer, has impressed during his loan spell at Celtic this season. He recently earned his first senior international cap for Belgium in a Euro 2016 qualifier against Cyprus.

Andros Townsend scored a great goal for England, silencing his critics. He said critics like Paul Merson helped push him to do well, especially during his time in Italy. This season has been tough for the 23-year-old player, who hasn’t reached the same level he showed when he first played for England. But manager Roy Hodgson still believed in him. That faith was rewarded in a big way at Juventus Stadium. Townsend scored England’s equalizer in a 1-1 friendly draw against Italy on Tuesday night. He celebrated the goal with his Tottenham teammates, Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

Chinese property company Dalian Wanda Group has officially bought 20% of Atletico Madrid. The deal was confirmed at an Extraordinary General Meeting on Tuesday. The legal team for Wanda Madrid Investment signed the agreement to buy 726,707 shares for €45 million (£32.8 million. This purchase was first announced in January, but two Extraordinary General Meetings were needed to complete it. Wanda Group chairman Wang Jianlin wants to grow Atletico Madrid’s brand in Asia. Atletico Madrid’s manager, Diego Simeone, is speaking to the media.

Antonio Conte returned to Turin for the friendly match against England, but he says he had very fond memories. He was Italy's new manager, replacing Cesare Prandelli in August after Italy failed to get past the group stage of the World Cup. His first seven months as Italy's manager have been very difficult. Italy needed a late goal from Eder to tie Bulgaria 2-2 last Saturday. Conte was also reported to have received death threats from Juventus fans after Claudio Marchisio got a knee injury the day before the Euro 2016 qualifier.

Ian Murray thinks that a potentially easier schedule could help Hibs overtake Rangers for second place in the Championship. His Dumbarton team has played both of his old clubs this season and will face them again in the final weeks. Although Rangers are currently in better form—beating Hibs and Cowdenbeath, while Hibs lost to Raith—Murray doesn’t think that will last. He believes the advantage could shift back to Hibs at Easter Road soon. Murray also thinks Rangers may not be able to keep up their current pace through the final month of the season.

Liverpool goalkeeper Simon Mignolet took photos with pilots in an airplane cockpit when he returned to England after playing in Belgium’s Euro 2016 qualifying matches against Cyprus and Israel. He was named in the match-day squad for both games, but did not play because Chelsea goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois was chosen instead. Mignolet has 14 international caps. He shared the photos from the cockpit on his official Facebook page on Wednesday. The pictures show Mignolet (centre) standing with the pilots.

A large country estate, including a Grade II-listed manor house and five cottages, is for sale for £6 million. The estate covers 200 acres of land near Bridgnorth in Shropshire. It has a swimming pool, tennis court, stables, and a cricket pitch. The main house, Chyknell Hall, has 11 bedrooms and was built in 1814. It has only been sold twice since then. The house is in the Regency style and is thought to appeal to famous people because of its private, secluded grounds. The estate is being offered for £6 million.

Two campus police officers in Dallas have been put on administrative leave after video showed them mistreating a group of four students. One student was hit and then arrested. The incident happened at El Centro College. A student named Charles Adams filmed the event on his phone. He was smoking a cigarette when he saw what happened. The officers approached the students, who were high schoolers waiting for a bus, outside the downtown Dallas campus. The video shows the officers acting aggressively.

Kilmarnock's interim manager Gary Locke has been made permanent after signing a three-year contract. Locke, 39, previously managed Hearts and joined Kilmarnock last summer as assistant to Allan Johnston. When Johnston left in early February, Locke took over as manager. Since then, he has lost only once in seven games. He will speak to the media at a press conference on Friday morning. After the deal was confirmed, Locke shook hands with club chairman Jim Mann.

One of the most important games in German football happens this weekend. Borussia Dortmund and Bayern Munich have shared the last five Bundesliga titles. Bayern are expected to keep winning the league this season. But this time, the two top teams are not close in the standings — Dortmund is 9 points behind and 9 places lower than Bayern. Still, the game is just as important as ever. Fans and players know that when these two teams play, it always matters. Jurgen Klopp, the Dortmund manager, celebrated with his players after beating Hannover.

A 14-year-old schoolgirl was left at a busy airport after easyJet refused to let her board its plane. She was carrying two pieces of hand luggage. Deva Joseph cried at London Stansted airport when she was told she couldn’t fly home to Spain. She offered to pay to check her second bag, but was told only credit cards would be accepted—even though she is too young to have one.

Gordon Robson, 26, killed his grandfather, John Potts, 45, with one hard punch to the back of the head. The punch was so strong it made a loud crack sound. This happened after Robson had been drinking at his grandfather's funeral. He was at a sports bar in Washington, Tyne and Wear, when he got into a fight. John Potts, a devoted father, tried to stop it. Robson then hit him, and he died. Robson had a past of violent behavior. He was sentenced to three and a half years in prison for the killing.

Scoring against your old team and making a perfect set-piece from training are two of the best moments in football. For Notts County player Ellen White, Thursday night was unforgettable because she did both at once against Arsenal in the Women's Super League. In the 26th minute, Notts County got a free kick near the box. Laura Bassett and Alex Greenwood nearly collided, causing confusion. Ellen White then spun near the box and kicked the ball straight into the corner of the goal, scoring against her former team.

High school girls in China are doing military-style dagger drills. They shout words like "kill," "stab," "slash," and "jab" as they do eight specific movements in a fast and intense training session. The girls, aged 16 to 18, are from the 27th March Huizhou Integrated High School. They are being trained by Inspector Tan, a former special forces soldier. Even though the drills involve knives, the knives are not real. The school official, Huang Anruo, confirmed that the daggers used are fake for safety.

We spend about one-third of our lives sleeping, but many of us don’t think about what our body and mind really need during sleep to feel rested. A new study by the Sleep Health Foundation found that 30 percent of Australians say they don’t get enough sleep every day. According to Professor David Hillman, not getting enough sleep means you have to make up for it, or else you won’t function well all week. The study also says most adults should get about eight hours of sleep each night, but seven to nine hours is normal.

A video has been shared on Facebook showing a fight between neighbours in a Perth suburb that turned violent. The clip shows an angry woman yelling racist insults over her fence at a group of men she appears to believe are of African descent. The woman then goes into her neighbour’s front yard, holding a metal crowbar. She shouts at the men and swings the crowbar at them. The men respond by picking up their own weapons, and a fight breaks out. The woman is heard saying, “I don’t deal with monkeys, go on now, you f*****g monkeys.”

A lot of people are watching 19-year-old Valencia left back Jose Luis Gaya. Manchester City, Arsenal, and Chelsea are all interested in signing him this summer. He’s a Spanish player who has played for Spain’s under-21 team. His buy-out clause is £13.5 million. That’s not too high, especially when you compare it to Luke Shaw, who was the same age and potential but cost £27 million. So it makes sense that English clubs would want him. But there are also concerns about whether he’s ready for the Premier League. Gaya played for Valencia in a La Liga game against Sevilla earlier this season.

Police in Oregon are asking the public for help identifying a motorcyclist who helped stop a man who allegedly threatened two teenagers with a gun. The incident happened in Salem. The man, Edward West, 59, is accused of pointing a handgun at the teens and saying, "get ready to die." Just then, a man on a green motorcycle arrived and used his helmet to knock the gun from the man’s hand. The teens were able to run away. The motorcyclist’s identity is still unknown.

Tim Sherwood is telling Ron Vlaar to show he still deserves to be Aston Villa's captain. Vlaar is coming back from injury and will play in the match against Manchester United at Old Trafford. He missed the penalty in the World Cup quarter-final against Argentina, but still played a key role as Holland reached the semi-finals. That performance made him a target for Manchester United. Now, with Villa fighting to avoid relegation, Sherwood wants Vlaar to prove he’s still a top player and not be forgotten.

Tim Sherwood says he is not worried about Aston Villa’s possible summer takeover. He plans to build a team that fits his style next season, as long as the club avoids relegation. Randy Lerner is reportedly talking to a potential buyer, and if a new owner takes over, questions may arise about Sherwood’s future. But Sherwood is concentrating only on helping Villa stay in the league. After that, he will work on his long-term plans during the summer. Sherwood, the Villa manager, says he is not concerned about the takeover talks. Christian Benteke scored and celebrated as Aston Villa beat Sunderland last month.

Celtic have long wanted Manchester City to let Jason Denayer return on loan to Parkhead next season. But City's manager, Manuel Pellegrini, said on Thursday that City's young academy players aren't ready to play in the first team. This means players like Denayer might have to come back early from loan deals. Jason Denayer has done well during his loan spell at Celtic this season.

Southampton manager Ronald Koeman is waiting for a clearer date for Fraser Forster's return before deciding if he needs to sign another goalkeeper in the summer. Forster had knee surgery after hurting himself badly during Southampton’s 2-0 win over Burnley two weeks ago. Doctors think he could be back in four to 12 weeks, but Koeman isn’t giving a firm date. He believes goalkeeper Kelvin Davis is good enough to cover for now, but he might have to bring in another keeper if Forster’s recovery takes longer than expected. Forster’s injury happened during the match against Burnley.

Rotherham manager Steve Evans was angry on the touchline during his team’s close Sky Bet Championship loss to Birmingham. Rotherham were fighting relegation and were denied a penalty. The home team had taken the lead in the first half through goals by Robert Tesche and Clayton Donaldson. Matt Derbyshire scored one for Rotherham, who were fourth from bottom. Later, Rob Kiernan handled the ball on the edge of the box, causing Derbyshire to fall inside the area. But referee Dean Whitestone did not give a penalty, which made Evans very upset. Birmingham then held on to win.

Virgil van Dijk is worrying about his chances with the Dutch national team. Holland has already let in more goals in five Euro 2016 qualifiers than they did in the whole World Cup qualifying campaign. And Guus Hiddink still hasn’t contacted him. Van Dijk was in two national team squads last year, but that didn’t lead to a real chance. When the Dutch drew 1-1 with Turkey, he was relaxing in the Arabian Gulf, hanging out with club teammates. He’s been playing well for Celtic, but still hasn’t been called up to the Dutch national team.
