Rangers' interim chairman, Paul Murray, said on Thursday that the club's removal from the stock exchange was completely due to actions taken by past board members. The club must leave the Alternative Investment Market (AIM) because it couldn’t find a new nominated advisor (Nomad) to meet rules. Murray also said the new board’s plans for the future won’t change and that planned investments will still happen.

Wayne Rooney and his England teammates were disappointed with how they started their match against Italy on Tuesday night. It was a friendly game at Juventus Stadium in Turin, nine months after they played each other in the World Cup. England had won seven games in a row, so many were hopeful. But in the first half, they played poorly and failed to create much. Italy scored first through a header by Graziano Pelle. England equalized later, making the final score 1-1. Rooney said he and the team were upset by their weak first-half performance.

Dundee United's board has responded to strong criticism from two major supporters' groups, Arabtrust and the Federation of Dundee United Supporters Clubs. The groups said they were shocked that 25% of the £6.3million spent on transfers for Ryan Gauld, Andrew Robertson, Stuart Armstrong, and Gary Mackay-Steven was paid as commission to unknown people. They also questioned chairman Stephen Thompson's claims about how much he has invested in the club. The board defended itself by highlighting the team's success on the pitch.

Gary Locke will be officially named Kilmarnock’s permanent manager on Friday. This is exactly eight weeks after he was asked to take charge until the end of the season. The club will make the announcement on Friday morning, and he will sign a three-year contract. The 39-year-old former Hearts manager also thanked the players for their hard work, which helped him gain the support of new chairman Jim Mann since he took over as caretaker manager in February, replacing Allan Johnston.

Chinese parents often want their children to become child prodigies, like 10-year-olds who go to university or 4-year-olds who copy Michael Jackson's dance moves. Now, a new young basketball star is becoming famous. A video is spreading online in China showing a small boy with amazing basketball skills—even better than some pro players. The boy is five years old and his name is Mai Zizhuo. He has been playing basketball since he was two and a half, according to People's Daily Online. The video begins with him scoring several baskets in a row, then running while dribbling two basketballs at once.

Bayern Munich will miss versatile left-back David Alaba for about seven weeks due to a torn knee ligament. Alaba, who had already been out for three months earlier this season with a partial ligament tear in his right knee, got injured during Austria’s 1-1 draw against Bosnia on Tuesday. He was tackled by Emir Spahic. The 22-year-old said he was " bitterly disappointed" but is focused on returning in time for the season's end.

Hull KR have signed experienced Australian forward Dane Tilse to replace Michael Weyman and Ryan Bailey, who both left the team. Tilse, who is 6ft 7in and weighs over 17stone, has agreed to a two-and-a-half-year deal with the Robins. He will join the club once he gets the required paperwork, after the Canberra Raiders agreed to release him. The 30-year-old has played 200 games in Australia. He will also be joining his old Canberra teammate, Terry Campese, who is now Hull KR’s captain and has signed a two-year contract extension. Tilse is taking over the same role that Weyman had, after Weyman retired last month because of injury.

Livingston manager Mark Burchill thinks midfielder Darren Cole wants to play in Sunday’s Petrofac Cup final, even though his cousin, Shaun Cole, died tragically just a week ago. Shaun, 22, was found dead on a Miami street. He was a soldier who had served in Afghanistan and was on leave in Florida. He had been to a music festival and was later found on the pavement with a head injury. Police believe he was hit by a car and killed. Darren Cole is grieving, but his manager hopes he will play in the final.

Alan Smith has denied reports that Liverpool fans attacked the ambulance he was in after he was seriously injured during Manchester United’s 0-0 FA Cup defeat to Liverpool at Anfield in February 2006. He broke his leg and disdised his ankle while trying to block a free-kick by John Arne Riise. At the time, some reports said fans threw bottles, beer glasses, and stones at the ambulance, and even rocked the vehicle as it was taking him to hospital. This content may be disturbing.

Celtic are interested in signing Hearts captain Danny Wilson this summer. He is a former Rangers and Liverpool defender. Celtic may offer £400,000 for him. Wilson has one year left on his contract. Hearts owner Ann Budge says the club doesn’t need to sell him. Hearts are not in a hurry to sell him, even though he will be out of contract at the end of the season.

Ronny Deila says Celtic won’t risk their Champions League hopes by doing another tough pre-season tour. He blames last summer’s busy schedule — including games in the US, Austria, and Germany — for their 4-1 loss to Legia Warsaw in the qualifying round. Celtic earn good money from these pre-season matches and have played in Australia and the Far East in recent years. Deila and player Nir Bitton left the pitch after the loss to Legia Warsaw. A return to the US this July is still possible, but not confirmed.

Franck Ribery has said that reports linking Wolfsburg's Kevin de Bruyne to a move to Bayern Munich are not true. De Bruyne, who was mostly on loan during his two years at Chelsea, has scored nine goals this season and leads the Bundesliga in assists with 16 – seven more than anyone else. But Ribery says that even though De Bruyne is playing well, he doesn’t fit the style of play that Pep Guardiola wants. He believes De Bruyne has different strengths than himself and his teammate Arjen Robben.

The girlfriend of an Arizona State University football player, Davon Durant, has now said she lied about being assaulted. She said her mood swings made her make up the story. Durant, a linebacker at ASU, was arrested on domestic violence charges after his girlfriend, Kelsi Langley, said he hit her in the face and choked her during an argument in his car on March 7. After the arrest, Durant— who came to ASU from a Kansas college and was a five-star recruit— was suspended from the football team indefinitely. He could also be expelled from the university.

What could be more exciting than meeting your idol? How about meeting your idol at a Starbucks, wearing a shirt with their name on it, and having your photo posted to their Instagram? One little boy got to do all that when he met Justin Verlander, the pitcher for the Detroit Tigers. Verlander took a selfie with the boy, who was wearing a dark blue shirt with Verlander’s name and jersey number, 35, on the back. The photo was shared on Verlander’s Instagram. See video below.

Eden Hazard said that playing so many games this season might have made him too tired to play his best. He was taken off after 62 minutes in Belgium’s 1-0 win over Israel. He has played 48 games this season for club and country, missing only five matches for Chelsea. He was a key player in their push for the Premier League title. During the match, Belgium had a tough time beating Israel. Hazard was substituted with 28 minutes left because he was struggling to beat his opponent, Orel Dgani. Belgium’s manager, Marc Wilmots, made the decision to take him off.

Police found 20 grams of marijuana hidden inside a leg of lamb in the Northern Territory. Something about the meat seemed strange, so the Northern Substance Abuse Intelligence Desk reported it. Officers then x-rayed the meat and discovered the drugs. The lamb was believed to have been sent to a company at Darwin Airport, and then planned to be shipped to the Tiwi Islands, about 100kms to the north.

Former Premier League footballer Clarke Carlisle has said he has separated from his wife, Gemma, after struggling with depression following a suicide attempt. He has moved out of their home in Yorkshire, where they had lived together for 14 years. Carlisle tried to take his life in December, just two days after being arrested on suspicion of drink-driving.

Arsenal legend Paul Merson had to admit he was wrong after criticizing Andros Townsend's call-up to the England squad. Townsend, a Tottenham winger, came on as a substitute and scored a brilliant equalizer in England's 1-1 draw against Italy in Turin. His goal was a strong response to Merson's comment in his Sky Sports column, where he said, "If Andros Townsend can get in, then it opens it up for anybody." The match took place on Tuesday night, and Townsend celebrated his goal with teammates Ryan Mason and Kyle Walker.

Cesc Fabregas, the Chelsea midfielder, has a habit of playing poorly in the second half of the season. He was one of the worst players on the field again in Spain's 2-0 loss to Holland on Tuesday. The 27-year-old said he was happy living in southwest London earlier in the week, but his performance has dropped a lot since around Christmas. When he was at his best, he looked like he would break the Barclays Premier League record for assists.

Six people have been arrested in Dover this morning on suspicion of terrorism offences linked to Syria, police said. The group includes five men and one woman. They were taken into custody around 8 a.m. in the departure area of the south coast port. Four of the men are from Birmingham and are in their 20s. The other two are a 26-year-old man and a 23-year-old woman, both without a fixed address. All six are being questioned at a police station in the West Midlands.

Get ready to buy something — the strongest urge to treat yourself happens today at 2:52pm. A study says that people in the UK spend about £62 each week on treats. This includes things like a chocolate bar, a glass of wine, or even expensive clothes and shoes. The study was done by the website VoucherCodes.co.uk. It found that people often want to buy something during lunchtime. Also, men spend about a third more each month than women on treats.

Arsène Wenger is so respected and clearly very smart that sometimes you agree with him, only to realize later that what he said sounds right but doesn't really hold up. This often happens after a bad defensive performance, when he points out that Arsenal’s defensive stats are actually good (which they are). But last week, he talked about player quotas—specifically, FA chairman Greg Dyke’s plan to raise the number of homegrown players in a Premier League squad from 25 to 2.

Charlie Austin has shared how his friend Joey Barton ignored him on his first day at Queens Park Rangers, not realising who he was. Later, they realised their mistake and became close friends. Austin has had a strong first season in the Premier League, scoring 15 goals, and is now being considered for the England national team. Although their friendship is well known, their first meeting is one Austin will never forget.

This dog saved his owner from a cold and muddy grave. The black dog was filmed at the Clarence J. Brown Dam and Reservoir in Springfield, Ohio, on Saturday afternoon. The man, whose name isn't known, was pulled to safety by firefighters after being stuck in water near zero degrees Celsius for almost two hours. He had gotten stuck waist-deep in mud while trying to recover some duck hunting gear. He was able to call 9-1-1 for help, but firefighters couldn’t reach him by boat because the river was too shallow.

Juventus coach Massimiliano Allegri says he doesn't expect the fans to fully accept him until he leads the team to a league title. He joined Juventus last summer, after being fired by AC Milan. Since then, he has done well, guiding Juventus to a strong lead in the race for the Serie A title. Allegri took over from Antonio Conte last summer. On Saturday, Juventus will play at home against Empoli, aiming for another three points. Juventus are currently first in Serie A, and Allegri is their manager, watching from the touchline.

Nathan Redmond had only been on the field for six minutes when he made a key play in this close match. Steven Whittaker saw the chance and passed the ball perfectly to Redmond down the right side, keeping it just inside the touchline. Redmond used his speed to quickly beat Joe Bennett. Then he sent a low cross to the back post, where Bradley Johnson scored. Johnson celebrated after scoring the winning goal in the second half at the Amex Stadium.

For people in Celoron, New York, the statue of local celebrity Lucile Ball is not funny. It has upset them for six years. In 2009, the town put up a statue of Ball. But many people were shocked and horrified by how she looks. The statue shows her in a way that many think is unflat and ugly. A Facebook group called "We Love Lucy! Get Rid of this Statue" has more than 600 likes. The statue is based on a scene from Ball's show "I Love Lucy," where she pretends to be drunk and sells a fake health tonic.

South Sydney hooker Issac Luke is facing a homophobic accusation after posting a rude comment on social media. The 27-year-old had posted on his Instagram to help find a young Rabbitohs fan who was attacked at ANZ Stadium in Sydney. The boy was hurt during a heated match and left in hospital. Luke said he wanted to give the boy a jersey as a kind gesture, especially before the Easter long weekend.

People who fear spiders should be careful — this might scare you. A man in Wangaratta, in northeast Victoria, was shocked when a large huntsman spider crawled out from inside his car door handle. The video shows him walking up to his black Holden Ute and spraying insect repellent on the door. The spray made the spider come out from under the handle. He calmly says, “Get out, you bastard.” But when the spider’s long, hairy legs suddenly appear, he screams and jumps back in fear.

Tottenham's manager, Mauricio Pochettino, says Harry Kane is like the great striker Gabriel Batistuta. He also says he'll be there to support Kane if he ever has a bad spell. Kane scored just 79 seconds after coming on in his first full England game, against Lithuania. That move him to within two goals of 30 for the season. England's manager, Roy Hodgson, is careful not to put too much pressure on Kane, who has risen fast. He only made it to Tottenham's first team after loan spells at Leicester and Norwich.

A former footballer who ran a £30 million investment scheme and lived like a millionaire has now fallen on hard times, a court has heard. Michael McIndoe played for Bristol City and Wolverhampton Wanderers. He convinced other footballers to invest by promising a 20% return. But the scheme failed, leaving him with over £2 million in debt. He was declared bankrupt in October last year. Once known as 'Mr Big' in Marbella, where he enjoyed a wild lifestyle with glamorous women, he is now struggling to get by and is being pursued by creditors in court.

Juventus director Pavel Nedved has said Barcelona are interested in signing Paul Pogba. In an interview with Mundo Deportivo, Nedved — who played 1124 games for Juventus — said Pogba will not be leaving the club. He also said he was happy Juventus did not face Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-finals. Nedved, a former Juventus player, confirmed the interest but stressed Pogba is staying at Juventus.

A man who has a criminal record for sex offenses was reportedly run over by his girlfriend after she said she caught him abusing a 2-year-old girl. James Oliver, 48, was seriously injured in the leg after being hit by a car driven by Linda Currier, 53. Police found Oliver in the driveway of a house in Noblesboro, Maine, on Saturday night, according to NBC News. Authorities said the couple had an argument inside the home after Currier saw Oliver allegedly trying to sexually harm the young girl.

Liverpool's target, goalkeeper Neto, is also wanted by PSG and several clubs in Spain, according to his agent, Stefano Castagna. Brendan Rodgers faces strong competition to sign the 25-year-old, who plays for Fiorentina. Liverpool were linked with Neto earlier in the season when Simon Mignolet was dropped. A move in January didn't happen, but Neto is now expected to leave Fiorentina in the summer when his contract ends in June. He was seen rushing from his goal during a match against Roma in March, as Juan Iturbe approached.

Not everyone should drive a $50,000 car. That’s the message from a video posted by YouTube user Richard Stewart. It shows a Porsche Cayman losing control right after a green light in Prince Edward Island, Canada. The car swings sharply from side to side before hitting a concrete barrier. One wheel flies off before the car stops. Stewart wrote on YouTube: "Just because you have a nice car doesn’t mean you’re a good driver. Don’t let your son drive your Porsche!"

If Rory McIlroy wins the upcoming Masters, he will complete a career grand slam, which has been a lifelong goal for the world’s top golfer. In partnership with his sponsor Bose, McIlroy has released a video showing his journey from playing on small courses as a child to becoming a world champion, including some tough moments along the way. The video starts with McIlroy jogging early in the morning, with the words "Six weeks to Georgia" on screen. It also includes an interview with a young Rory McIlroy before he became famous in golf.

Sergio Garcia says he is focused on winning his first PGA Tour title since 2012 at this week’s Shell Houston Open. Even though the Masters is coming up soon, and there’s a lot of talk about Rory McIlroy trying to win his third major in a row to complete a career grand slam, and whether Tiger Woods will come back from his break from golf, Garcia is not distracted. He is only thinking about ending his winless streak. The Golf Club of Houston has a course setup similar to Augusta, but Garcia is staying focused on his own goal. He was seen lining up a putt during the Cadillac Championship in Doral, Florida, last month.

Riki Hughes, a former Iraq war soldier, has been jailed for 16 months after stealing £17,000 from a children's football club where he volunteered as club secretary. He used the money for personal things, including camping gear and a stag trip to Las Vegas. The court heard he lied about using the money to pay rent, even though the club was already getting its property for free.

Johnny Sexton has become very used to success. Winning big trophies has become a regular part of his life. He has added many major wins to his record over the years, and he is determined to keep doing it. Just before a European Champions Cup quarter-final game against Saracens in Paris, the 29-year-old Racing Metro player and Irish international looked back on his career. He said he was lucky to have played with strong teams like Leinster and Ireland, and that he hasn’t missed out on winning a trophy in most years. In fact, the only year since he started playing at senior level when he didn’t win a major trophy was 2010.

Mustafa Kamal stepped down as ICC president on Wednesday. He said India influenced the result of the Cricket World Cup quarter-final between Bangladesh and India. He made the comments at the airport after returning from the tournament in Australia. Kamal, who is from Bangladesh, said everyone could see what happened in the Bangladesh-India match. He accused India of using its position in the ICC to affect the game's outcome. He also said he would have reacted the same way if any other country had been treated this way. Mustafa Kamal, who is pictured with the Cricket World Cup trophy, is now a former ICC president.

West Ham manager Sam Allardyce has defended Nigel Pearson and said he respects him for being true to himself. Allardyce worked with Pearson when he was manager of Newcastle United in 2007. Now, they will meet again when West Ham plays Leicester City at the King Power Stadium on Saturday. Pearson has been in the news for several controversial moments this season, including grabbing Crystal Palace’s James McArthur by the throat and losing his temper during a press conference. Leicester City manager Nigel Pearson has been involved in a number of controversial incidents this season.

Skipper John O'Shea is urging Sunderland to win their fifth straight derby against Newcastle. The match takes place on Sunday at the Stadium of Light. Sunderland have won the last four meetings, but they badly need three points to stay clear of the fight to avoid relegation from the Premier League. If Burnley beat Tottenham earlier in the day, Sunderland could drop into the relegation zone. That would make winning the match absolutely essential.

Stoke manager Mark Hughes says it's time to stop losing at Chelsea's stadium. Since Stoke got promoted to the Barclays Premier League in 2008, they have played Chelsea away in all competitions eight times and have lost every match. Their last win at Stamford Bridge was in 1995, in a League Cup game. Since then, they haven’t earned a point there — not even a draw — since a 1-1 draw in 1984. The most recent game was a 3-0 win for Chelsea, with Frank Lampard celebrating.

Newcastle are hoping to avoid a third straight loss when they play rivals Sunderland in Sunday’s important derby. They’ve been struggling lately, especially since striker Papiss Cisse was banned. Newcastle are at the bottom of the Premier League, just one point above the teams in the relegation zone. But according to Sportsmail, if it weren’t for Cisse’s goals, Newcastle would actually be two points further down, right in the relegation zone. Cisse is Newcastle’s top scorer this season with 1 goal, and 10 of his goals have been important in turning games in the team’s favor.

For Ronny Deila, qualifying for the Champions League isn’t just about money. But now there are 16 million reasons for the Norwegian to get Celtic there — by winning the league for a fourth year in a row. And all of those reasons are about money. This week, UEFA announced the new payment system for the next three years of European football. The last time Celtic played in the Champions League group stage, in 2013-14, they played against AC Milan, Ajax, and Barcelona. They won one game and earned £12.6 million. Tottenham defender Ben Davies says he won’t let personal feelings get in the way when he plays against his Wales teammate Sam Vokes at Burnley on Sunday. Tottenham are going to Burnley’s Turf Moor ground after one defeat in their last four Premier League games — a loss to Manchester United. They want to keep their good form going and stay in the race for a European spot. Burnley are fighting to avoid relegation and are currently 8th, just one point above the danger zone. Earlier this season, in the FA Cup, Sam Vokes scored for Burnley against Tottenham at Turf Moor, and after the equalizer, Ben Davies turned away.

Neil Redfearn is thinking about whether he will stay as manager of Leeds United after the club suspended his assistant, Steve Thompson, on Thursday. Leeds took two months to hire Thompson, but yesterday morning, he received a letter from director of football Nicola Salerno saying he would be suspended until the end of the season. This means he will not stay at Leeds United after just 105 days. He has also been told that the club will not choose to renew his contract when it ends.

John Carver says he might use a whip to motivate his Newcastle players before Sunday’s Tyne-Wear derby at the Stadium of Light. Newcastle have lost the last four games against Sunderland. Carver, who was assistant to Alan Pardew during those losses, admits Sunderland played harder than Newcastle in those matches. He said, “In the last four games, Sunderland have outworked us – and that’s not a good sign.” He added that he will “whip” his players to make sure they’re ready and motivated to beat Sunderland on Sunday.

David Templeton has strongly criticized the training methods used at Rangers under Ally McCoist and Kenny McDowall. He said Stuart McCall, who joined on a short-term deal last month, has brought a new style of coaching and better tactical preparation than under the previous management. Templeton praised McCall’s positive impact, saying the team’s two recent wins have boosted confidence ahead of Saturday’s home game against Hearts, who won the Championship title. The Rangers winger is very positive about McCall’s effect since he arrived.

Celta Vigo player Nolito says Lionel Messi should not play in Sunday’s La Liga game. Messi has a foot injury but has been training and is expected to be fit. Nolito, 28, joked that Messi should just go to the beach instead. He told Marca: "I guess he'll come, but he can spend the day at the beach as far as I'm concerned. I'll give his dad a call in a minute." Messi is expected to play for Barcelona against Celta Vigo after recovering from the injury. He was seen training with teammate Javier Mascherano on Thursday.

Robbie Neilson says players like captain Danny Wilson will only leave Hearts if he thinks it’s the right move for the club. As Sportsmail reported, Celtic have listed Wilson, a former Rangers defender, as a possible summer signing. Before Sunday’s Championship game against Rangers, Neilson said it’s natural for top players to attract interest from other clubs. But he insists he won’t sell any players unless he agrees it’s the right decision for Hearts. He also agrees with owner Ann Budge that any departures must be approved by him, and only if the price is right.

Blackpool are talking about signing Austria defender Thomas Piermayr, who is 25. He has been training with the Championship club this week. Blackpool want to bring him in, and it is expected he will join for next season, which will be in League One. Piermayr is a free agent and previously played for Colorado Rapids. He once played for Inverness Calt. in 2011. He has never played in England before, so a Blackpool deal could be his first chance to play there.

Tony Pulis wants to talk to West Bromwich Albion chairman Jeremy Peace after the team is safe in the Premier League. He believes the club has gone wrong in recent seasons and needs big changes to return to being a top-1ten team. West Brom finished 10th and 8th under Roy Hodgson and Steve Clarke, but then struggled last season and ended up 17th. The team’s manager, Tony Pulis, was seen shouting instructions from the sideline during a match against Manchester City.

Arsenal legend Ian Wright is upset that Theo Walcott might leave the club. He thinks Walcott hasn't played well because Arsene Wenger won't let him play as a striker. Walcott has only started five games this season after missing seven months due to a serious knee injury. Now, with Arsenal looking to sign Raheem Sterling and Walcott's contract ending next summer, Wright fears the team could lose a key player.

Roberto Martinez believes Ross Barkley can become an even more important player for Everton and England. Barkley had a mixed season with Everton, affected by a knee injury that delayed his return to action, and he was also part of England’s squad for last summer’s World Cup. However, England manager Roy Hodgson still trusts him. Martinez is encouraged by Barkley’s two recent substitute appearances for England — against Lithuania and Italy — which show he’s ready to improve again.

England will not play in the Under-19 European Championships this summer after losing 2-1 to France in their final qualifier. England had won their first two matches in the Elite Round, against Denmark and Azerbaijan. They needed to beat France in Saint-Lo to qualify for the finals in Greece in July. But France scored through Sehrou Guirassy and Gnaly Cornet, taking the lead. Fulham's Patrick Roberts scored late for England, but it wasn't enough. The Young Lions failed to qualify.

Newcastle midfielder Jonas Gutierrez is hoping to mark his return to first-team football with a win in the local derby against Sunderland. The 3-year-old Argentinian has come on as a substitute in each of the last three games since recovering from testicular cancer. He has been warmly welcomed back by teammates and fans. But he’s been on the losing side in all three matches. Now, he wants to end that streak. Newcastle are trying to recover from their worst run of four straight losses to Sunderland, and the game is on Sunday at the Stadium of Light.

After a close game between South Sydney and Canterbury at ANZ Stadium in Sydney on Good Friday, the Rabbitohs won 18-17 in the final minute. The match ended in controversy when referees penalized Bulldogs captain James Graham. The decision upset many fans. As the referees, officials, and players were leaving the field, some fans threw plastic water bottles at them and shouted insults.

Kevin Sinfield, the former England rugby league captain and legendary Leeds Rhinos leader, has been told he may become a target when he moves to rugby union. The 34-year-old announced suddenly that he will leave rugby league at the end of the season. He will join Yorkshire Carnegie, the sister club of Leeds Rhinos, on an 18-month contract. This move means he will switch from rugby league to rugby union.

Raheem Sterling says he isn’t ready to sign a new contract with Liverpool, even though he was offered a £100,000-a-week deal. The 20-year-old winger said in a BBC interview that he would have accepted a much lower wage just a year ago. Although he is one of Liverpool’s key players, Sterling hasn’t played as well this season. He has scored only six goals, which is one fewer than Stoke’s Jon Walters. Brighton and Hove Albion are teaching their young players about the law and ethics of sexual consent. They are the first football club to offer this kind of training to youth players, according to the BBC. The programme, called Protect, Inform and Prevent ( PIP), explains what legally counts as consent. The training includes private Q&A sessions where players can talk about past experiences. These sessions are led by a former police detective and a psychotherapist.

A new video shows homeless people reading mean tweets that were written about them. The video was made by the creative agency Leo Burnett Toronto for the charity Humans For Humans. It aims to make people think differently about people who sleep on the streets. Many of the people cry while reading messages like, "I hate the homeless, I don’t feel sorry for you," and "I saw a homeless girl across the street. I almost vomited." The video is meant to show how hurtful words can be.

George Boyd is the hardest-working player in the Barclays Premier League this season, running 210.5 miles. This is the same distance as running from Burnley’s Turf Moor stadium to Crystal Palace’s Selhurst Park in south London. He has run a little more than Tottenham’s Christian Eriksen. Normally, walking that route would take 69 hours, but Boyd covered it in less than 40 hours of actual playing time. George Boyd is the Barclays Premier League's hardest working player, clocking up 210.5 miles on the pitch.

Police have arrested the parents of a five-month-old baby who died yesterday. The baby, from Perry Barr in Birmingham, was taken to Birmingham Children's Hospital after being found unresponsive. She had breathing problems, and police were called to the home just before 1 a.m. The child died later that day. The father, 25, and mother, 25, were both arrested. Police say the death is suspicious, and a post-mortem exam will be done today to find out exactly what caused it.

Raheem Sterling is not being disloyal to Liverpool by delaying talks about a new contract, says player's chief Gordon Taylor. The 20-year-old England player has been offered what manager Brendan Rodgers called an " incredible" deal, believed to be £100,000 a week. But no agreement has been reached, and talks have stalled. Sterling says he is not just after money, and Taylor, who is also the head of the Professional Footballers' Association, thinks waiting until the end of the season to continue talks could be smart. Sterling also said in a TV interview that he is not ready to sign a new contract with Liverpool.

Anderson hasn't done well since leaving Manchester United to go back to Brazil. On Wednesday, he was sent off in the first half for pushing a striker, Otacilio Neto, from Ypiranga Erechim, even though the push happened when the ball wasn't in play. The striker hit back with an elbow, so he was also sent off. But Anderson was lucky because his teammate, Fabricio, got a red card too for swearing at the fans. That made Internacional play with only 1 player left, as they already had 2 red cards. The game ended 1-1 in Porto Alegre.

A seven-year-old boy was raped and set on fire by two teenagers after he went to buy food. The teenagers took him to a remote area and raped him. When he tried to fight back, they set him on fire, police said. The boy, who had burns covering 80% of his body, managed to escape. The incident happened in Padma Nagar, Bhiwandi, a suburb of Mumbai. Police are investigating the case.

A pug named Dug has made a surprising recovery after being bitten in the face by a rattlesnake. Dug and his owner, Lindsay Castro, were hiking on the Jurupa Hills trail in Fontana, California, on Thursday. They heard a rattling sound, so Lindsay stepped back. But Dug ran toward the noise—and got bitten. The snake bit him on the face, and his face quickly swelled up to twice its normal size.

Jose Mourinho might one day surprise everyone by returning to manage Real Madrid, even after his difficult departure, says Real Madrid defender Alvaro Arbeloa. Mourinho left Real Madrid after three years to go back to Chelsea in 20013. He left under a cloud, with reports of arguments with key players like club captain Iker Casillas, Sergio Ramos, and Pepe. But Arbeloa, who has played 25 times for Real this season, says the door will always be open for Mourinho to come back as manager. So, Mourinho could still return to Real Madrid one day, says Arbeloa.

Liverpool's hopes of qualifying for the Champions League ended on Saturday at the Emirates. The manager, Brendan Rodgers, admitted in a short press conference that their chances were gone. He didn't hide that the season had been tough. After coming close to winning the title last year, Liverpool are now out of the race. It's a hard result for a club that had hoped to return to greatness. Rodgers stayed positive, as he always does, but he didn't pretend the season was a success. Still, the team seems to be making progress under him.

Inter Milan coach Roberto Mancini was angry after his team drew 1-1 with Parma, who were at the bottom of the league. He cancelled the players' Easter day off and made them train early on Sunday morning at 8 a.m. The first team trained as confirmed on Inter's website, www.inter.it. Club vice-president Javier Zanetti and sporting director Piero Ausilio were at the training session. Mancini was upset with how the players played and their attitude. The draw left Inter joint ninth with Genoa, 10 points behind the teams that qualify for European football.

Most fans want to own a special piece of memorabilia from their favourite player or team. Small parts of sports history can sell for thousands of pounds. But you might be surprised to learn that an old passport belonging to Paul Parker — best known for playing as a right back for Manchester United and England in the 1990s — was listed on eBay for £5,000. The item was put up for sale earlier in March, and bidding ended on Tuesday. It’s not clear if anyone actually paid that much for it. Paul Parker, a former Manchester United and England defender, once had this passport, which is now on eBay.

He has been seen in toast, pancakes, crisps, and even ice cream. But a builder was shocked when he saw Jesus Christ on a piece of wood just a few days before Easter. Paddy Morrall found a full picture of Jesus on a broken scaffolding board in Inverness, Scotland, on Wednesday. The board had been left out in the rain for several hours. Jesus was shown wearing a robe. Paddy Morrall, a 3-year-old builder from Keighley, near Bradford, has kept the board.

Ondrej Duda scored in the second half to give Slovakia a 1-0 win over the Czech Republic on Tuesday in a friendly match. The 20-year-old midfielder scored with a low shot from outside the penalty area in the 49th minute — his second goal for Slovakia. This was Slovakia’s third win in 10 matches against the Czechs since the split of Czechoslovakia in 1993. The Czechs have won five of those games. Martin Skrtel was shown a yellow card for kicking Daniel Kolar in the face with a high boot during the match. Slovakia players celebrated their 1-0 win, which continues their strong recent performance.

Karim Benzema showed he’s more than just a football player. The Real Madrid star shared a video of himself rapping while driving his Bugatti Veyron. The video came as Real Madrid gets ready to play Granada in La Liga on Sunday. In the clip, Benzema sings along to Tupac’s song 'Check Out Time'. A better song choice might have been 'All Eyez on Me', since Benzema is trying to score more goals. So far this season, he has scored 0 goals in all competitions. Benzema, who plays for Real Madrid and France, is showing off his singing skills in the video.

A wealthy businessman who supports UKIP, Harvey Boulter, is trying to stop a popular Conservative candidate from winning. Boulter already gave £30,000 to the UKIP candidate running against Liam Fox in Somerset. This is part of a long-running personal fight against Fox, whom Boulter helped force out as Defence Secretary. Boulter is also spending another £30,000 to try to beat Tom Tugendhat, a top Tory candidate, in Tonbridge and West Malling, Kent.

In the last four minutes of the Yorkshire derby between Sheffield Wednesday and Huddersfield, two goals led to a 1-1 draw. Sheffield Wednesday’s substitute, Sergiu Bus, scored in the 86th minute. Then, Huddersfield’s substitute Ishmael Miller equalised with a goal in the 90th minute. The draw means Huddersfield have not won in their last seven games. They are now 18th in the league, nine points and six places behind Sheffield Wednesday. Sergiu Bus celebrated by scoring the goal that put Sheffield Wednesday ahead.

Stuart Dallas has come a long way since Mark Warburton found him playing part-time on a muddy field for Crusaders in Northern Ireland, where he was earning just £70 a week. The 23-year-old, who had a strong performance for Northern Ireland earlier in the week, scored two brilliant goals as Brentford beat Fulham 4-1 on Good Friday. Brentford now head into their match against Nottingham Forest on Monday with ambitions beyond just a play-off spot. This is not the same player who was spotted three years ago — he’s now a key part of Brentford’s push for the Premier League. His two goals against Fulham were a highlight of a strong season.

Baseball is often seen as America's favorite pastime, so it's not surprising that many people feel strongly about their favorite professional team. The two most famous and historic teams are the New York Yankees and the Boston Red Sox. They are the top two teams in popularity, with the Yankees ranked first and the Red Sox second when it comes to fans who say they are their favorite. The Texas Rangers and Atlanta Braves also have a large number of fans, especially in the southern U.S. But some teams don't have as many fans—like the New York Mets. Scroll down to watch the video.

A high school basketball star has won hearts by asking a girl with Down syndrome to be his prom date. Trey Moses, a senior at Eastern High School in Louisville, Kentucky, is going to play college basketball at Ball State next year. He surprised Ellie Meredith during her P.E. class with flowers and a sign that said, "Let's Party Like it's 1989"—a nod to Taylor Swift’s album, which is Ellie’s favorite. Trey, who volunteers with teens who have learning disabilities, asked her to the prom. Ellie happily said yes and shared that she’s excited to go dress shopping because she’s already told "about a million people" about it. She spoke about the moment to CNN.

On April Fools' Day, President Barack Obama joked around by pretending to be the fictional president Frank Underwood from the TV show *House of Cards*. He wore a fake mustache and looked like the character, who is played by actor Kevin Spacey. Obama said, "Hello everybody. This is not Frank Underwood. This is Barack Obama. Happy April Fools' Day. Frank learned it from me." He also spoke in a Southern accent, just like the character does. The video of the joke was shared online.

Caykur Rizespor midfielder Ludovic Obraniak was taken to the hospital on Saturday after he was substituted during a match against Fenerbahce. He had to leave the game after only 30 minutes because of a possible heart problem. Obraniak, who is from Poland, was on loan from German club Werder Bremen. The club said on social media that he was not in any immediate danger after initial tests. Moussa Sow scored for Fenerbahce during their 5-1 win on Saturday.

Three people were taken to hospital after a head-on crash between a vintage 1973 E-Type Jaguar and a Toyota Kluger. The accident happened on Easter Sunday night at a traffic light intersection on Warringah Road in Frenchs Forest, northern Sydney. The Jaguar, believed to be worth more than $120,000, was completely destroyed in the crash. No one was hurt in the collision, but all three adults were sent to hospital as a precaution. NSW police are still looking into what caused the crash.

People in Lijin village, in Dongying city, Shandong Province, China, have been seen carrying natural gas in large plastic bags. The bags are as long as six metres. They are moving the gas on rickshaws. Pictures show this happening often. Some people are worried because natural gas can explode if it comes near a flame or even a cigarette. This is dangerous. Local news says people do this to save money on gas transport. It is common in some villages.

Tiger Woods has been seen hitting golf balls on the practice range at Augusta National, which is raising hopes that he might play in this year’s Masters. He hasn’t played on the PGA Tour since pulling out of the Farmers Insurance Open on February 5 due to a back injury. Since then, he’s taken time off to recover and get back to his best. There’s been talk he might come back for the Masters, a tournament he’s won four times. He was seen practicing at Augusta on Tuesday and has returned to the course. This week, he also dropped out of the top 100 in the world rankings for the first time in nearly 19 years.

The BBC has been criticized for spending thousands of pounds of licence fee money on a four-page guide about how to use emojis. The guide was made after BBC bosses asked an agency to study how smiley faces could be used in news stories and on social media. The BBC also paid for emoji designs of famous people like Gary Lineker and Graham Norton. At the same time, the BBC used a sad face emoji to describe the death of the world’s oldest woman.

One of the world’s top long-distance runners and a frequent training partner of Mo Farah says he is scared for his life. He says he has reported serious abuse by a coach in his home country of Uganda. The coach is accused of sexually abusing female runners, some as young as 15. The runner, Moses Kipsiro, who won the 10,000m title at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow last year, said five female runners came to him for help. Since then, he says he has received death threats after reporting the abuse to Uganda’s national sports federation and police.

Patrick Kluivert, a former Dutch footballer and assistant coach, has started his time as Curacao’s coach with a win in the 2018 World Cup qualifiers. Curacao moved on to the second round of CONCACAF qualifying. The team drew 2-1 in Montserrat in the second leg, winning 4-3 on aggregate. Curacao had already won 2-1 on Saturday in Willemstad. Kluivert, who once worked with Louis van Gaal at the 2014 World Cup, helped lead Curacao to the next stage.

An 18-year-old college student who was caught on video biting the head off a live hamster has been kicked out of his fraternity, stopped attending college, and sent for a mental health evaluation. The video, filmed during a drunken Spring Break party in Florida, shows the student, Brady Eaves, laughing as he kills the animal. Eaves, who was raised by a former Mississippi governor candidate, is now facing possible felony animal cruelty charges. If convicted, he could go to jail for up to five years and pay a $500 fine.

Sri Lanka's sports minister, Navin Dissanayake, said Kumar Sangakkara should think again about retiring from limited-overs cricket and play for one more year. Sangakkara ended his one-day international career on March 18, after losing in the World Cup quarter-final. He said he was sad about the loss but happy that Sri Lanka is in a better position now than when he started in 2000. The minister told reporters that he respectfully asks Sangakkara to serve the country for another year. This came after the minister appointed a new temporary group to run cricket, led by former test player Sidath Wettimuny.

Edinburgh have brought back three Scotland internationals — Dougie Fife, Alasdair Dickinson, and Ross Ford — for Sunday's European Challenge Cup quarter-final against London Irish. The players were rested for last week's Pro12 match against Scarlets, which Edinburgh won 26–15 in Llanelli. They had played for Scotland in the RBS Six Nations before that game. Head coach Alan Solomons has now recalled them, hoping to name his strongest team. Dougie Fife is one of three Scottish players returning after Six Nations duty. In a separate image, England's Courtney Lawes is tackled by Scotland's Ross Ford and David Denton.

Chris Ramsey says Tony Pulis is one of the best British coaches, but he doesn’t think he needs to learn from him. Ramsey’s QPR face Pulis’s West Brom at the Hawthorns on Saturday. QPR are 19th in the Premier League, four points behind Sunderland in 17th. Since the start of the year, QPR have only earned four points. They need a strong finish, like Pulis did in 2013-14 with Crystal Palace, when his team got 17 points from their last eight games to avoid relegation. Ramsey spoke positively about Pulis ahead of the important match.

An 18-year-old girl, Silhan Ozcelik, has appeared in court. She is accused of planning to travel abroad to join Kurdish rebels fighting against the Islamic State. She went missing from her family's home in north London last October, when she was 17. The court heard that she traveled on the Eurostar to Stuttgart, Germany, with another man. Stuttgart is where the youth wing of the Kurdish Workers’ Party (PKK) is based. Silhan Ozcelik, a sixth-form student, is also accused of preparing to carry out a terrorist attack in October 2014.

Leicester City midfielder Esteban Cambiasso knows what it's like to win football's biggest trophies. He says saving Leicester from relegation would be one of the best moments of his career. Cambiasso played for Inter Milan, where he won five Serie A titles and also won the Champions League in 2010. He is a former Argentina international. He joined Leicester last summer on a free transfer and signed a one-year contract at the King Power Stadium. He told the BBC on Thursday that avoiding relegation would feel just like winning a trophy.

Crystal Palace manager Alan Pardew says Manchester City still have a chance to win the Barclays Premier League title, even though they are behind. Last season, City came from behind to beat Liverpool and win the title, and in 2012, Sergio Aguero scored in stoppage time to beat Manchester United and win the title on goal difference. Right now, Chelsea are six points ahead at the top of the league and have one game left to play, but Pardew says the race isn't over. He's speaking after his team, Crystal Palace, beat Stoke. Pardew says he won't rule out City winning the title, even though they're behind. His team plays City on Monday.

Hull City has asked the Football Association again to change the club's name to Hull Tigers, after the first request was rejected. This upset fans who thought the club would keep its current name, especially since the FA council voted 7 to 7 against the change. But now, Hull City manager Steve Bruce has confirmed the club has made another application to the FA to rebrand as Hull Tigers. If owner Assem Allam gets his way, Hull City will become Hull Tigers. Allam still wants the name change, even though fans are angry. An arbitration panel has now said Allam can apply again.

Before Saturday's Premier League game between Swansea City and Hull City at the Liberty Stadium, Sportsmail will give you all the key details. This includes team news, possible player lists, betting odds, and statistics from Opta. Here is what you need to know about Swansea's home game against Hull. Swansea will wait until late on Saturday to decide if Ecuadorian winger Jefferson Montero can play.

A man who lost his sight 12 years ago has found a passion for painting and can now make impressive pictures just by touching them. John Bramblitt, 42, had epilepsy starting at age 11, and over the next 19 years, it slowly took away his eyesight. He became completely blind at age 30. Even though he can't see, he chose not to let that stop him from painting. He uses a special method: first, he applies fabric paint to make a shape or outline, then adds color. He is from Denton, Texas.

 team news.

 Chelsea. Chelsea are still deciding whether Diego Costa will play in Saturday's match against Stoke. He hurt his hamstring in their previous game, a win at Hull. He also missed Spain's international duty. Even though he has been cleared to play, he might not be used because of the injury risk.

Ibrox has been a tough place for Rangers this season, with three visits from Edinburgh clubs and three losses. Hearts beat Rangers 2-1 in August, and Hibernian won 3-1 and 2-0. Rangers manager Stuart McCall says his team now must repay their fans by winning when Hearts visit Ibrox on Sunday. A 2-0 win at Easter Road two days ago could have been a turning point in Rangers’ struggling fight for promotion.

If you like complicated plots and mystery, avoiding Paisley last night might have seemed like a smart choice. Celtic, who are chasing a Treble, were playing against St Mirren, who were struggling and close to falling apart. It didn’t seem likely to be an exciting game. But even though Celtic won in the end, this match showed clearly that they won’t easily win their fourth straight league title. Celtic winger Kris Commons (on the right) tried to score during the SPL game against St Mirren on Friday.

Ulster have signed Charles Piutau, a New Zealand international. Piutau, 23, can play at full back, wing, or centre. He will join Ulster on a two-year deal starting in July 2016. He has 14 caps for the All Blacks and made his Test debut against France two years ago. He has played for the Blues in New Zealand since 2012. Ulster team manager Bryn Cunningham said signing someone with Piutau’s talent is very exciting for the team.

Alessandro Diamanti and Mohamed Salah helped Fiorentina beat Sampdoria 2-0 in a rainy match, moving Fiorentina into fourth place with 49 points. Diamanti scored just after the 60th minute, and Salah scored again two minutes later. The loaned Chelsea player, Salah, also scored in Fiorentina's win. In another match, Miralem Pjanic scored the only goal as AS Roma beat Napoli 1-0, their first home win in over four months. Salah also continued his good form, scoring again in the match.

Juventus moved closer to winning a fourth straight Serie A title with a 2-0 win over Empoli on Saturday. Carlos Tevez scored just before halftime, and Roberto Pereyra added a second goal in stoppage time. Juventus now lead the league by 14 points with nine games left. A fourth straight title is within reach.

Kevin de Bruyne's agent has said there is no deal for him to leave Wolfsburg this summer. However, he admitted that several clubs are watching the Belgian midfielder. De Bruyne has become one of the most sought-after players in Europe after doing well in the Bundesliga. He has been linked with Manchester City and Bayern Munich. In an interview with FOCUS Online, his agent Patrick De Koster said that many clubs are interested and there has been some informal talk, but no transfer has been agreed.

Swansea manager Garry Monk wants to get his first point of the season against Hull on Saturday, after the international break. Swansea have had a strong season, staying in the top 10 all year, and are now in eighth place. They are close to their best-ever Premier League points total. They have eight games left and need five more points to beat the 47-point mark from their first Premier League season in 2011-12. During a training session this week, Monk pointed to his striker, Bafetimbi Gomis.

Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo are known as two of the greatest football rivals today. But former Brazil striker Ronaldo says he'd like to see both of them play together on the same team. He's a co-owner of Fort Lauderdale Strikers, a football club in the second tier of the United States. Ronaldo wants to make his team a big global name. He says he'd even spend his own money to sign Messi. He also hopes to bring Cristiano Ronaldo to his team.

Northampton will wait for expert advice before deciding when George North will play again. He will miss Saturday’s European Champions Cup quarter-final against Clermont Auvergne due to a head injury. George North has been knocked unconscious three times in recent months, including in last Friday’s match against Wasps. He was seen by a neurologist on Wednesday. Northampton’s director of rugby, Jim Mallinder, said, “We won’t play him at the weekend.” He added that North had a serious knock and was unconscious for a short time after being hit during the match against Wasps.

Cesar Azpilicueta is waiting for the final few games before Chelsea win the Barclays Premier League. He believes the team has proven their strength by staying at the top of the league since the start of the season. Chelsea are currently first in the table, ahead of their match against Stoke City at Stamford Bridge on Saturday. They are six points ahead of second-place Manchester City, and they have one game more than them. Chelsea have been seen as strong title contenders all season. Azpilicueta says this is because they started so well in August — winning seven of their first eight games, which helped them take the lead early. Cesar Azpilicueta (center) is counting down the games until Chelsea win the Barclays Premier League title.

Mohamed Diame is set to return from injury when Hull City play Swansea on Saturday. The Senegalese midfielder, who joined Hull for £3.5 million from West Ham in the summer, has been out for over four months with a knee injury. Hull manager Steve Bruce confirmed Diame will play part in the game. He said Diame is physically strong and in great shape, but had a serious injury. His return is a big help for Hull, who are fighting to avoid relegation.

Toby Alderweireld will go back to Atletico Madrid when his loan from the club ends at Southampton. The 26-year-old Belgian defender has played well this season in south England. He has previously said he might like to stay in the Premier League,, and Tottenham are also interested in him. But Atletico Madrid say they expect him to return, along with Oliver Torres, who has been playing in Portugal with Porto.

Swansea's England Under 21 player Tom Carroll may be out for up to six weeks because of ankle ligament damage. He got injured during England's 1-0 win over the Czech Republic last Friday. The injury happened just after he scored the only goal in the match, which took place in Prague. Carroll, who is on loan from Tottenham, has made 18 appearances for Swansea this season. After scoring, he was surrounded and celebrated by his teammates.

Franck Ribery says he won’t be able to play against Borussia Dortmund this week because he hasn’t recovered from his injury. He admits he "can't even run" right now. He limped off during a game against Shakhtar Donetsk at the start of last month. That game also saw Bayern Munich’s other winger, Arjen Robben, get injured. Ribery is hoping he might be back in time for the German Cup quarter-final against Bayer Leverkusen later in the week.

Bayern Munich captain Philipp Lahm may play in the Bundesliga game against Borussia Dortmund on Saturday, after recovering from an ankle injury. However, coach Pep Guardiola confirmed that several key players are still out: Franck Ribery (ankle), Arjen Robben (stomach), Javi Martinez (knee), and David Alaba (knee). Guardiola also said he’s not sure if defender Holger Badstuber (hip) will be fit. Midfielder Thiago Alcantara might play for a few minutes, as he recovers from a long-term knee injury. Lahm has fully recovered from his broken ankle. Bayern will be missing many first-team players for the match against Dortmund.

Michael Duff, a long-time defender for Burnley, thinks manager Sean Dyche could one day manage the England national team. Dyche, who is 43, has built a strong reputation since he joined Burnley in October 2018. He turned the team around, proving many wrong by leading Burnley to promotion from the Championship to the Premier League last season. Duff is now preparing to play against Tottenham in the Premier League on Sunday. He still believes Dyche has what it takes to manage England one day.

Mauricio Pochettino has allowed Harry Kane to play in the European Under-21 Championships this summer. Roy Hodgson has confirmed that Kane will be in Gareth Southgate's squad for the tournament in the Czech Republic. Kane will also go to Australia and Malaysia before the championships. He made his senior England debut last week, coming on as a substitute and scoring against Lithuania. He then started in the match against Italy. Despite his recent senior debut, Kane will play for the Under-21 team in the European Championships.

Alvaro Morata wants to keep developing at Juventus and does not want to go back to Real Madrid, says his agent, Beppe Bozzo. The 22-year-old moved to Juventus last summer for £ 15.8million after not getting enough chances to play regularly for Real Madrid. He signed a five-year contract with Juventus after starting only three games in La Liga for Real during the 2013-14 season. Morata is happy at Juventus and has no interest in returning to Real Madrid. he has also done well since joining, scoring seven goals in 22 Serie A games this season.

Hundreds of football fans are in for a tough weekend due to train service cuts over Easter. Many Premiership and Championship games are planned for the long weekend, but large parts of the train network will be closed for repairs. Over half of the games will likely face delays and problems, pushing fans to drive instead. The big Premiership match between Arsenal and Liverpool in London will also be affected by the train disruptions. Labour says the government didn’t learn from the Boxing Day chaos, when almost a million fans had terrible travel experiences.

Brentford manager Mark Warburton was happy after his team won 4-1 against Fulham in a tough west London derby at Craven Cottage. Stuart Dallas scored two goals, and a great free-kick from substitute Alan Judge, plus a late goal from Jota, gave Brentford the three points. With six games left, Brentford are now fifth in the league with 69 points and still in the running for a playoff spot. Warburton said he was really pleased with the team's performance.

The Barclays Premier League has announced the final list of televised matches for the 2014-15 season. Sky Sports and BT Sport have both shared their broadcast plans, with the race for Champions League spots being a key focus. The matches between Chelsea and Liverpool on May 10 and Manchester United vs Arsenal on May 17 are the most important live games. The TV schedule for the last day of the season, Sunday, May 24, will be announced later. Juan Mata scored for Manchester United in a live TV game against Liverpool last month. Manchester United also beat Arsenal earlier in the season at the Emirates. The match on Saturday, May 2, at 12.

A 70-year-old American P-51D Mustang fighter jet has been carefully rebuilt from over 200 parts by father-and-son builders Bill and Scooter Yoak. This jet, which once served in combat, was restored as a tribute to American soldiers who died in war. The restored jet now soars through the sky in breathtaking on-board video, proving the hard work and dedication of the two men who brought it back to life.

Brazil's World Cup stadium in Natal is for sale. The company that owns it, Grupo OAS, is having money problems. This is because of a corruption scandal involving the state oil company, Petrobras. The company is also trying to sell its 50 percent share in another stadium, the Fonte Nova in Salvador. Grupo OAS has been struggling for months to get loans and funding since the corruption investigation started. A photo shows the Dunas Arena in Natal during a World Cup game between Italy and Uruguay last year.

A group of 13 U.S. senators has written to FIFA, asking it to remove Russia as host of the 2018 World Cup. They say Russia should not host the event because of its role in the Ukraine crisis and its occupation of Crimea. The senators, who are from both the Democratic and Republican parties, strongly urged FIFA to move the tournament to another country. The letter was dated Tuesday and made public on Wednesday.

Five people, including Thomaz Alckmin—the son of São Paulo’s governor, Geraldo Alckmin—died when a helicopter crashed into a house in the Carapicuiba area, on the outskirts of São Paulo. The crash happened yesterday at about 5.20pm local time. The helicopter struck a residential home, killing five people.

Jos Hooiveld scored late in the game to give Millwall a vital 2-1 win over Charlton, their first victory at The Den since October. Magaye Gueye equalised with a low shot after Alou Diarra had put Charlton ahead. Charlton’s captain Chris Solly was sent off in the first half for deliberately handling the ball in the penalty area. Millwall’s goalkeeper Stephen Henderson saved Lee Gregory’s penalty kick. Gueye then scored the winning goal in the 87th minute, and celebrated with a teammate.

This year, the hatchback turns 50. It might not be as fast as a Ferrari or as fancy as a Rolls Royce, but it’s the most popular car in the world. The hatchback was first made to help French farmers carry sheep to market. Now, two out of every three cars sold in the UK are hatchbacks. They are also very popular in cities like Munich and Mexico City because they are practical, fuel-efficient, and comfortable. The first hatchback ever made was the Renault 16, which came out in April 1965. The Renault 4, which came before the Renault 16, was originally designed to help French farmers carry sheep.

Venezuela captain Juan Arango has apologized after biting a rival player, Jesus Zavala, during a heated Mexican league match. Arango’s team, Tijuana, was losing 4-3 to Monterrey with only seconds left. He bit Zavala on the shoulder. Arango, a 34-year-old midfielder, said he did something wrong by biting Zavala. Zavala, who was playing for Monterrey, showed the referee the bite mark on his shoulder. Monterrey won the game 4-3.

Paul Merson has再次 criticized Andros Townsend after Townsend came on for Tottenham in the 83rd minute of their 0-0 draw with Burnley. Merson posted on Twitter: "Just been watching the game, did you miss the coach? #RubberDub #7minutes." Merson had previously upset Townsend with a comment in his Sky Sports column, where he said that if Townsend can make the England team, then anyone could.

Cristiano Ronaldo's decline has been overstated. The Real Madrid player scored five goals against Granada, bringing his La Liga total to 36 for the season — more than half of Europe's top teams have scored this season. Real Madrid won 9-1 at the Bernabeu, with Ronaldo leading the charge. This was the first time in his career he scored five goals in one game. His 36 league goals beat Lionel Messi's 32, and now he has scored more goals than 53 of the 98 teams in Europe's top five leagues this season.

England are likely to qualify for the Euro 2016 finals, but manager Roy Hodgson still seems unsure about his best starting team. Sportsmail’s team of reporters has each picked their own England XI for the tournament in France, assuming all players are fit. Share your own England team in the comments below. England manager Roy Hodgson was seen at Juventus Stadium during Tuesday’s friendly match against Italy. MATT LAWTON'S XI: Hart; Clyne, Cahill, Jagielka, Baines; Henderson, Wilshere; Welbeck, Rooney, Sterling; Kane.

Hull recovered from their loss to Hull KR on Thursday to pull off a surprise 28-20 win at Langtree Park, leaving St Helens with a third straight defeat. Jamie Shaul scored a long-range try that proved enough to win, shocking the home fans who thought their team was struggling after a tough match on Good Friday. St Helens, already missing players due to injury, had another tough week after losing to rivals Wigan. They started the game with two teenage debutants in the three-quarters, and Hull saw an opportunity to exploit weaknesses. Fetuli Talanoa (left) celebrated his try against St Helens as Hull secured the unexpected win.

Almeria, who have been struggling in La Liga, have appointed former Barcelona player Sergi Barjuan as their third coach this season. The 43-year-old Barjuan takes over from Juan Ignacio Martinez, who was fired on Sunday after Almeria lost 4-1 at home to Levante. Almeria said that if all the paperwork is finished, Barjuan will coach the team in their away match against Barcelona on Wednesday. Barjuan, a former Barcelona defender, played 53 times for Spain between 1998 and 2004. He spent nine years at Barcelona as a player and also played in two World Cups for Spain. He previously coached Recreativo in Spain’s second division from 2012 to 201

Easter Sunday is coming, and Christians across America observed Good Friday, which remembers the crucifixion and death of Jesus Christ. In places like Ohio, Pennsylvania, and over the Brooklyn Bridge, people took part in "Way of the Cross" walks. These were just a few of many events happening around the world as Holy Week, which started on Palm Sunday, comes to a close. Tens of thousands of people attended Pope Francis' Good Friday torchlight procession at the Colosseum in Rome. The pope used the service to highlight the persecution of Christians.

While England fans were having a few drinks at the Huntsman pub in Turin on Tuesday afternoon, many went outside to sing an anti-IRA song. The song, which says "**** the IRA," was repeated many times. Inside the Juventus Stadium, where about 3000 England fans were sitting in the north-west section, the same thing happened. England fans sang anti-IRA songs during the friendly match against Italy, which ended in a draw. There is no evidence that the fans in the photo were part of the singing.

Most ads in newsagents' windows are for things like pets or handyman services. But one man, known only as John, used the space to find love instead of using online dating. John, a builder, put up a personal ad in the window of his local newsagent in Muswell Hill. The ad, written in big black letters, said he was looking for someone special and offered "a way of life with quality." A passerby saw the ad, took a photo, and shared it online. The post quickly spread and became popular.

Helsinborg's manager Henrik Larsson had to put his 42-year-old kit man, Daniel Andersson, in goal on Saturday. Two of the team’s regular goalkeepers, Par Hansson and Matt Pyzdrowski, were injured, so there was no choice. Amazingly, Andersson kept a clean sheet as Helsinborg drew 0-0 with Kalmar in the opening game of the Allsvenskan season. After the match, Andersson — who is a retired goalkeeper and once played one game for Sweden in 2001 — said to local TV: "It was a situation I never thought I’d face. Going from kit man, to goalie coach, to playing in goal."

Ben Jones-Bishop scored a great solo try in a close match that ended 24-18. Salford Red Devils broke a streak of 17 straight losses to Wigan. The win moved Salford up to third in the league. Jones-Bishop, who joined Salford from Leeds Rhinos in the summer, now has seven tries this season and is the team’s top scorer. Salford led 12-8 at halftime. Jones-Bishop scored in the 60th minute to help secure the win. The match was very heated, and both teams had 12 players on the field at the end after several players were sent off.

It has been just over a year since Alan Pardew had a bad argument with Manuel Pellegrini on the touchline while managing Newcastle. The FA warned Pardew about his behaviour, and he later wrote to Pellegrini to apologise for calling him an offensive name. On Monday at Selhurst Park, Pardew—now manager of Crystal Palace—will face Pellegrini and Manchester City again. He has made changes to stop a pattern of behaviour he thought was harming his work. After getting advice from the League Managers’ Association, the 53-year-old has had sessions with Jeremy Snape, a former international cricketer who now works as a sports psychologist.

Before this weekend's Premier League games, Sportsmail will give you all the key details for each match, including team news, squad lists, betting odds, and stats. Here’s what you need to know for Crystal Palace’s home game against Manchester City at Selhurst Park.

  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
  
**Team news: Crystal Palace**  
Crystal Palace manager Alan Pardew has no new injuries to report before the game against Manchester City. However, Marouane Chamakh and Fraizer Campbell are still out with hamstring injuries. Jordon Mutch is also not fit due to a thigh problem.

The title race might seem decided to some, but Joe Hart remains hopeful. He’s paid to believe, but there’s a good reason for his optimism. Manchester City won the league in 2012 and 2014 by making late, dramatic comebacks. Hart said, “That’s kind of how we do it.” When asked about needing to close a nine-point gap, he said, “We like to do it a different way.” He admitted the team hasn’t been at the level they wanted every week, but he believes football gives you a fresh start. That new chance begins on Monday against Crystal Palace. He also said they have eight important games left to reach the standard they need.

Mils Muliaina, a rugby player who won the World Cup, has been released on bail after being arrested on suspicion of sexual assault. The 34-year-old former All Black, who says he did not do anything wrong, was arrested last night. His team, Connacht, had just lost 14-7 to Gloucester in the quarter finals of the European Challenge Cup. Muliaina had been taken off the field earlier because of an injury. Police approached him at Kingsholm Stadium. He was later taken away by officers. The incident the police are investigating happened in Cardiff in March. Muliaina has played 1000 caps for the All Blacks.

QPR are feeling confident ahead of their important Barclays Premier League match against Aston Villa on Tuesday. They had lost 13 of their last 14 away league games, but won 4-1 against West Brom on Saturday. That win ended a five-game losing streak. QPR are still in 19th place, just three points from safety. Coach Chris Ramsey said his players need to stay calm, even after the win. Eduardo Vargas (center) celebrated with teammates after scoring the first goal against West Brom. After the match, Ramsey said, "It's a fantastic victory for us. The mood is good, and the team has stayed very professional."

Lydia Ko shot a 2-over 74 on Saturday at the ANA Inspiration. This was her second straight round over par, after she had tied the LPGA Tour record for most consecutive rounds under par at 29. The day before, she hit into the water and bogeyed the 18th hole, finishing with a 73. On Saturday, she made an 8-foot birdie putt on a par-5 hole, keeping her streak alive. Arsene Wenger hasn't decided yet if he will offer Abou Diaby a new contract, but he has hinted that Diaby might still have a future at Arsenal after this summer. Diaby played in a practice match on Wednesday, marking his latest return from injury. However, he has only played 22 games in the last five seasons at Arsenal, spending much of that time on the sidelines due to injuries. Arsenal will play Liverpool on Saturday in a midday match. Wenger probably won’t start Diaby in this important game, but he did say Diaby could earn a new contract, possibly one where he only gets paid when he plays.

Tiger Woods and Rory McIlroy aren’t in the field, but that hasn’t hurt attendance at the Shell Houston Open. A record number of people have come to the small town of Humble. The event, which is the last tournament before the Masters, is drawing big crowds. Fans are enjoying the fun and entertaining style of Phil Mickelson and local favorite Jordan Spieth. It’s been 18 months since Spieth left college to join the PGA Tour, even though he was ranked 809th in the world. Now, at just 21 years old, he’s ranked fourth in the world. And this time, no one is criticizing him.
